Step 1.1 chunking language remains in effect only when Step 1.2.5 activation conditions are not met.\n\n### Step 1.4 — Stage 1 Gate\n\nAll must pass before marking Stage 1 complete:\n\n| Gate | Requirement |\n|------|-------------|\n| G1 | File inventory table covers all diff entries |\n| G2 | Every distinct function scope and top-level declaration in every `@@` hunk has its own CC entry; `DEL` and `TABLE` constructs always get standalone CCs (per 2nd-pass rules of active REVIEW_PATH) |\n| G3 | Every `.c`/`.h` has INF resolved or `INF: ⚠️ not found` |\n| G4 | ELINK table present or noted as skipped |\n| G5 | Call graph present or noted as skipped |\n| G6 | CC Registry complete in context memory — all files and constructs registered |\n| G7 | CC Registry persisted — `$SESSION_DIR/cc_registry.md` when `RUNTIME_MODE = DISK`; context memory when `MEMORY-ONLY` (see Step 1.1.2 and Constraint precedence) |\n| G8 | PCD cache table and ELINK cache table both present in context memory (or explicitly noted as `[SKIPPED]` or `[PCD-CACHE: SKIPPED — no SDL/KEY/PCD content in diff]`) |\n| G9 | Unit test review mode resolved — `IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW` recorded in context memory (`TRUE` or `FALSE`) |\n| G10 | Chunk Plan written to `cc_registry.md` header with all chunk rows at `pending` status and `ACTIVE_CHUNK = C1` recorded in context memory — OR — `[CHUNK-PLAN: SKIPPED]` recorded when activation conditions are not met |\n\n**Unit test review mode (G9) — explicit user tag required:**\n\n`IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE` when **either** of the following is true:\n1. The user's initial review request contains one of the following inline tags (case-insensitive):\n   - `[unit-test]`\n   - `--unit-test`\n   - `unit test review`\n   - `review unit test`\n   - `unit-test-review`\n2. Step 0.2C resolved `ACTIVE_TAGS` to include `Unittesting` (i.e., the prompt contained `SourceTag: Unittesting`).\n\n**Default when neither condition is met:** `IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = FALSE` — even if the diff contains `*UnitTestHost.c`, `*UnitTestMock.c`, or other unit test files. Presence of unit test files in the diff does NOT auto-activate this mode.\n\n**When `TRUE` via inline tag:** Record `[UNIT-TEST-REVIEW: ENABLED — inline tag detected: \"<matched tag>\"]` in context memory.\n**When `TRUE` via SourceTag:** Record `[UNIT-TEST-REVIEW: ENABLED — SourceTag: Unittesting resolved at Step 0.2C]` in context memory.\n**When `FALSE`:** Record `[UNIT-TEST-REVIEW: DISABLED — no user tag in request]` in context memory. Step 3.10 will be skipped entirely.\n\nThis value is immutable for the remainder of the session.\n\n**Spot-check requirement:** Before leaving Stage 1, verify at least 3 cached entries from different categories. Record `Stage 1 Spot Checks: <passed>/<checked>` in context memory.\n\n### Step 1.5 — Context Memory Contract\n\nA missing **Required** record → abort and restart Stage 1. Stage 2 Cache Verification and Step 3.0 both verify this list before proceeding.\n\n**Required (Stage 1 → Stage 2):**\n- File entry (one per diff file): #, path, STATUS, ±lines, INF, MODULE_TYPE, Priority\n- CC entry (one per construct): CC ID, File, Category, Symbol, Lines, Description\n- INF-DELTA entry (empty table if none): File, API Call, Expected GUID, INF Section, Status\n- Agent State: Stage, FILE#/total, FINDINGS C/M/m/I, FP\n- Resume State: current stage, next CC or file pointer, last valid checkpoint *(inferred from `cc_registry.md` Review Status and `<!-- end-file-N -->` anchors in `Detailed_Review_Report.md`; no standalone resume record is stored)*\n- Chunk Plan state: `ACTIVE_CHUNK = C<N>` and immutable chunk boundaries (or `[CHUNK-PLAN: SKIPPED]`) — required when `REVIEW_PATH = Full` AND reviewable CCs > 80\n\n**Optional (emit fallback tag if missing — continue only when the current CC/IDV does not depend on this cache):**\n- PCD cache entry → `[PCD-CACHE MISSING]`\n- ELINK cache entry → `[ELINK-CACHE MISSING]`\n- Call graph entry → `[CALL GRAPH NOT BUILT]`\n\n**Required (Stage 2 → Stage 3):**\n- Agent State totals (C/M/m/I counts) — in context memory\n- INF-DELTA reachability notes (`[INF-DELTA-CONTEXT-REACHABLE: ...]`) — in context memory\n- All per-file finding sections flushed to `Detailed_Review_Report.md` — on disk (or equivalent content in context memory when `RUNTIME_MODE = MEMORY-ONLY`)\n- All CC `Review Status` values updated in `cc_registry.md` — on disk (or equivalent content in context memory when `RUNTIME_MODE = MEMORY-ONLY`)\n\n---\n\n## Stage 2: Per-CC Code Review\n\n> **Scope:** Review each CC from Stage 1 context against UEFI 2.10+/PI 1.8+/EDK II 2.2+.\n\n> 🧪 **Unit test mode — activate when `IS_UNIT_TEST_REVIEW = TRUE` (resolved at Step 0.2C via `SourceTag: Unittesting`, or at Stage 1 Gate G9 via inline tag):** When the user has explicitly requested unit test review, the following **must not be flagged** as violations during CC evaluation — these are valid and mandatory unit test patterns:\n> - `MODULE_TYPE = HOST_APPLICATION` — valid; no `[Depex]` required; not a firmware module\n> - `.cpp` source files — valid for GoogleTest; C++ idioms, constructors, and templates are allowed\n> - `extern \"C\" {}` wrappers around EDK2 `#include` directives in `.cpp` files — **mandatory** pattern; never flag\n> - `UT_ASSERT_*`, `will_return()`, `expect_value()`, `check_expected()`, `EXPECT_CALL()`, `TEST()`, `TEST_F()` — standard framework calls from `UnitTestLib` / cmocka / GoogleTest\n> - `#include <cmocka.h>`, `#include <Library/GoogleTestLib.h>`, `#include <Library/FunctionMockLib.h>` — framework dependency includes; not unknown symbols\n> - `MOCK_INTERFACE_DECLARATION`, `MOCK_INTERFACE_DEFINITION`, `MOCK_FUNCTION_DECLARATION`, `MOCK_FUNCTION_DEFINITION` — `FunctionMockLib` macros; not violations\n> - `#ifndef CONSTANT / #define CONSTANT value / #endif` guards in `*UnitTestHost.c` for Token.h constants — correct replacement pattern (Rule #6)\n> - Missing `[Depex]` in a `HOST_APPLICATION` INF — valid; `[Depex]` is not applicable to this module type\n> - No `EFIAPI` on C++ test functions — valid; C++ uses its own linkage convention\n>\n> **Severity cap:** All `HOST_APPLICATION` unit test file findings are capped at **MAJOR** maximum. Do not assign `CRITICAL` to unit test code unless confirmed that the module is included in a firmware binary (verify FDF/DSC inclusion chain before escalating). The `/unit-test-review` skill is loaded in Stage 3 Step 3.10 for comprehensive unit test standards validation.\n\n### Step 2.0 — Stage 2 Initialization & Per-File Flush Protocol\n\n**Cache Verification:** Validate all **Required** records per §1.5. Missing required → abort to Stage 1. Missing optional → emit fallback tag per §1.5; if the current CC depends on it, resume Stage 1 for that cache only. Stage 2 must not re-derive caller lists, ELINK prototypes, or PCD values on its own.\n\nIf recovery data exists, resume from the newest valid Stage 2 checkpoint instead of restarting from the first file.\n\n**Execution order:** By file priority (P1 first), then by CC sequence within each file.\n\n**Chunk isolation — applies only when `[CHUNK-PLAN: REGISTERED]`:** Load only the CC entries for `ACTIVE_CHUNK` into active context. Do not load CC details from other chunks. After all files in `ACTIVE_CHUNK` are fully reviewed (Phase A → B → C complete for every file in the chunk):\n1. Execute the normal per-file flush sequence for each file in the chunk.\n2. Update `cc_registry.md` Review Status for every CC in `ACTIVE_CHUNK` (one batched write per file, as normal).\n3. Compress all in-memory CC details for `ACTIVE_CHUNK` to a single aggregate line: `Chunk C<N> (files #<A>–#<B>): <c>C/<m>M/<n>m/<i>I — flushed`.\n4. Update the Chunk Plan header in `cc_registry.md`: set `ACTIVE_CHUNK` row status to `done`.\n5. Record `[CHUNK-COMPLETE: C<N> — files #<A>–#<B>, <c>C/<m>M/<n>m/<i>I]` in context memory.\n6. Advance `ACTIVE_CHUNK` to the next `pending` chunk. Load that chunk's CC entries from `cc_registry.md` on disk. Continue.\n\n**Cross-chunk findings:** When a finding's IDV Step 2 requires evidence from a file in a different chunk (already flushed), tag the finding `[CROSS-CHUNK: C<A>↔C<B> — <symbol or brief description>]`, record with `Confidence: MEDIUM`, and continue. Do not delay writing the finding. Stage 3 Step 3.1.0 resolves these.\n\n**Interrupt recovery within chunk:** Resume from the first `cc_registry.md` entry with `Review Status = NA` within `ACTIVE_CHUNK`. Do not restart from C1.\n\n**Before each file:** Re-read its Stage 1 entry (MODULE_TYPE, INF, priority) from the **context memory CC registry**.\n\nMismatch between cached and *passively observed* MODULE_TYPE (encountered during Phase A reads, not actively re-derived) → record as MAJOR finding `[⚠️ TYPE-DRIFT]` and continue using the more-restrictive of the two types.\n\n**Per-file flush sequence:** After all CCs for a single file are reviewed (Phase A → B → C complete for that file), perform the flush sequence before moving to the next file:\n\n1. **First file only — must** create `Detailed_Review_Report.md` with the full preamble — commit/patch header (from Stage 1 Step 1.0 data), Agent State block (running totals), and file inventory table (from Stage 1 cache). The full CC registry lives in `cc_registry.md` only — **do not** duplicate it in `Detailed_Review_Report.md`. Then **must** append this file's finding section below the preamble.\n2. **All files — must** append this file's finding section to `Detailed_Review_Report.md`. The section format: `## File #N: <path>` header, then CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR findings in severity order, then an `#### Informational Notes` subsection for INFO items. **Must terminate every per-file section with the HTML anchor `<!-- end-file-N -->`** (where N is the file's inventory number) — this anchor is required for Stage 3.1.7 INF-DELTA late finding insertion and interrupt recovery. **Must not** use `create_file` on this existing document — doing so overwrites all prior findings. *Note: review documents must not be processed by Markdown tools that strip HTML comments; doing so will break late-finding insertion and interrupt recovery.*\n3. **Must** update `cc_registry.md` — change `Review Status` from `NA` to the result for each CC of this file (one batched write per file, not per individual CC).\n4. Compress this file's in-memory CC detail to a single aggregate line: `File #N <path>: <c>C/<m>M/<n>m/<i>I — flushed`. **Must not** discard finding records from context memory before they are flushed.\n5. **Must** increment `FILE: #<N>/<total>` in Agent State.\n\n**Flush applies in all `RUNTIME_MODE` states** (see Review Document for `RUNTIME_MODE` definition).\n\n**Token budget — context compression:** For patches >30 files or >25 open findings, after each per-file flush compress all `[✅ PASS]` CC entries for the just-flushed file to the aggregate line above. **Never discard finding records.** If total in-memory CC detail entries exceed 200, or the current file has more than 25 open (uncompressed) findings in memory, immediately flush all completed CCs for the current file so far and update `cc_registry.md` for those CCs, then tag the event as `[CONTEXT-FLUSH: mid-file at CC <ID>]` and continue with the remaining CCs of that file. **Override when `[CHUNK-PLAN: REGISTERED]`:** PASS compression is governed by chunk boundaries only (Step 3 of the chunk isolation sequence above) — the `>30 files` and `>25 open findings` compression triggers are superseded and must not fire mid-chunk.\n\n### Step 2.1 — Per-CC Review Protocol\n\nFor each CC entry (one at a time, in priority order):\n\n#### Phase A — Read Context:\n1. Read the modified lines identified in CC registry plus surrounding context. For the **first hunk** of each `.c`/`.h`/`.inf`/`.dec` file, extend the read range to cover at least line 20 to capture the copyright and `@file` block:\n   - `FUNC-DEF`: read the **full function body** + caller sites from Call Graph when a graph is required (all inner changes — local vars, macros, includes, comments — are covered by this read)\n   - `STRUCT`/`TABLE`: read full declaration + all references in the same file\n   - `DEL`: read the deleted code and the surrounding code that remains\n   - `FILE-SCOPE`: read lines ±10 around the change or the enclosing file-scope block\n   - `.inf`/`.sdl`/`.dec`/`.fdf`/`.vfr`/`.asl`: read the full changed section\n2. For P1/P2 files: also read INF `[Sources]`/`[LibraryClasses]` and call sites only when the finding depends on cross-module ownership, lifecycle, or boundary analysis.\n\n**Phase A read budget:** Aim to keep each CC read within a practical range. If a required read is truncated or times out, record `[PHASE-A-TRUNCATED]` or `[PHASE-A-TIMEOUT]`, reduce confidence as appropriate, and continue unless the missing content is required for a blocking finding.\n\n#### Phase B — Review Every Modified Line:\n\n> Apply Pre-Finding Gate (see Constraints section) before opening any finding.\n\nReview each modified line in dimension order. Engineering judgment — not a mechanical checklist; apply the severity model to any suspicious pattern not explicitly listed.\n\n**Review Dimensions §1–§13:** Apply the dimensions defined in the `## Review Dimensions §1–§13` section of this agent. All `§<N>` references resolve to that section.\n\n#### Phase C — Accumulate per-CC in Context Memory; Flush Per-File to Disk:\n\nAfter each individual CC — before moving to the next CC — **must** record the result in context memory. After **all CCs for a file** are complete, **must** execute the per-file flush sequence (Step 2.0).\n\nAfter each individual CC:\n\n1. **Must record in context memory** for every CC, one at a time:\n   - If no issues: mark CC as `[✅ PASS]` with one-line summary in memory\n   - If issues found: record each finding using the format below\n2. **Must** mark CC status in memory: `[✅ PASS]` / `[🔷 MINOR-A]` / `[🔷 MINOR-B]` / `[🔶 MAJOR]` / `[🔴 CRITICAL]` / `[🛑 CRITICAL – ABORT TRIGGER]`\n3. **Must** update Agent State counts in context memory: `FINDINGS: <C>C/<M>M/<m>m/<I>I`. When an IDV verdict = `FALSE POSITIVE` is recorded: **must** also increment `FP: N` in Agent State immediately.\n4. **INF-DELTA context reachability** *(INF-DELTA Pipeline — Stage 2: Reachability Annotation)*: For `FUNC-DEF` CCs where a `[INF-DELTA-SCOPE: context]` entry exists for the same enclosing function, and the Phase A read confirmed the API call is reachable from the entry point of that function, **must** record `[INF-DELTA-CONTEXT-REACHABLE: <API> called in <FunctionName>]` in context memory. Stage 3 Step 3.1.7 consumes this note to promote that entry beyond LOW confidence.\n\n##### Finding Formats:\n\n> **Location links:** In every finding, populate the `Location` field as a Markdown link.\n> - Use the **Resolved Line** from the CC Registry. For `git diff`/staged/uncommitted inputs this is the `+L<N>` hunk offset; for commit/patch inputs it is back-filled from the Stage 2 Phase A function-body read.\n> - Format: `` `FunctionName()` [<basename>:<line>](../../<repo-root-relative/path/file.c>#L<line>) ``\n> - The `../../` prefix is required because the report lives at `.github/reviews/` — two directory levels below (nested within) the workspace root; `../../` navigates up to the workspace root where source files reside (e.g., a file at `AmiModulePkg/Foo/Bar.c` line 47 → `` `Bar()` [Bar.c:47](../../AmiModulePkg/Foo/Bar.c#L47) ``).\n> - **Accuracy check (verify for all findings before advancing to the next CC):** Confirm (a) the link path exactly matches the file's workspace-relative path from the diff header, (b) the `#L<line>` number equals the Resolved Line recorded for that CC in the registry — not the diff hunk context offset, (c) the display text `<basename>:<line>` uses the filename only (no directory), and (d) `FunctionName()` matches the enclosing function where the changed line resides.\n> - If Resolved Line is still blank when writing a finding, read the relevant lines of the file now (as part of the mandatory Phase A context read) and record the line before proceeding. Do NOT emit a finding with a placeholder or guessed line number.\n\nCRITICAL / MAJOR / MINOR:\n```\n#### Finding: [F<N>] – [SHORT TITLE]\n- **File:** `path` | **Severity:** [SEV] | **Confidence:** HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW\n- **Location:** `FunctionName()` [file.c:N](../../relative/path/to/file.c#LN)\n- **Observation:** [what is wrong]\n- **Violation:** [\\<Spec Name\\> §X.Y.Z — \\<normative rule text\\>; for AMI/project conventions: \\<convention name and source\\>]\n- **Fix / Improvement / Enhancement:** [concrete action — verb phrase; state exact change required, e.g., \"Add bounds check before CopyMem at line 47\"; mark `[ARCH-CHANGE REQUIRED]` if redesign needed; mark `[ENHANCEMENT]` for non-blocking hardening suggestions]\n<details><summary>IDV: F<N></summary>\n1. Context read → function body · call sites · INF [Protocols/LibraryClasses/Pcd/PcdEx] · PCD gate · MODULE_TYPE check\n2. Cross-module scope → <search results or N/A>\n3. Spec verdict: CONFIRMED / FALSE POSITIVE / UNVERIFIED\n</details>\n```\n\nINFO: `ℹ️ [F<N>] <path> — description. Suggestion: action.` (batch under `#### Informational Notes`, placed at the end of the containing section after all CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR findings)\n\n##### IDV Protocol (Inline Deep Verification):\n\n**Must** be executed for every CRITICAL and MAJOR finding before that finding is recorded — skipping IDV on any CRITICAL or MAJOR is a Prohibited Action. **MINOR-A** findings must use IDV-Lite by default; escalate to full IDV only when the finding crosses a trust boundary, depends on external ownership, or cannot be resolved locally. **MINOR-B** findings must skip IDV entirely — record with one-line rationale and tag `[🔷 MINOR-B]`; no IDV block permitted. INFO: no IDV required.\n\n**Abort Trigger findings:** self-confirming — Step 3 verdict is always `CONFIRMED {spec: UEFI 2.10+ / PI 1.8+}`. Steps 1 and 2 still run to establish `Confidence: HIGH`.\n\nFixed 3-step template — execute in order, no skipping:\n1. **Context read** — confirm you have read: (a) full function body, (b) call sites from Call Graph, (c) INF `[Protocols]`/`[LibraryClasses]`/`[Pcd]`/`[PcdEx]`. If any unread, read now before step 2. Additionally: (d) if changed hunk contains `#if TOKEN` / `#if PCD` guards, verify the resolved value from Stage 1 PCD cache — if the guarded path is compiled out in the build configuration, mark `[GATE-RESOLVED: PCD/TOKEN]` and do NOT open the finding; (e) compare the MODULE_TYPE observed during this read to the Stage 1 cached value — if they differ, record `[TYPE-DRIFT]` and use the more-restrictive of the two types for Step 3.\n   - **Gate after Step 1:** If the live context shows the finding is out of scope for the module type or build configuration, close it as `FALSE POSITIVE` immediately and skip Steps 2–3.\n2. **Cross-module scope** — apply the sub-rule that matches the finding type. **Sub-rule priority:** when a finding spans multiple categories, apply the most restrictive sub-rule only (Security–SMM > Security–intra-module > Lifecycle > ELINK > VFR/ASL > all other non-security). Never stack multiple sub-rules on the same finding.\n   - **Security — SMM / Standalone MM boundary / protocol / auth** (SMM isolation, Standalone MM isolation, `EFI_MM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL`, protocol install/uninstall, `VariableLock`, image verification bypass, phase constraints, DMA): `deep-search` cross-package consumers via protocol GUID. Dynamic caller cap by protocol criticality:\n     - **P1 security protocols** (SMM dispatch, MM dispatch, Secure Boot, auth, capsule validation, `EFI_SECURITY_ARCH_PROTOCOL`, `EFI_SECURITY2_ARCH_PROTOCOL`): cap at 5 callers\n     - **P2 standard protocols** (all others): cap at 3 callers\n     - If cap hit → `[CALL GRAPH CAPPED: <actual>/<cap>]`, `Confidence: MEDIUM`. Timeout → `[⚠️ CALL GRAPH MAY BE INCOMPLETE]`, `Confidence: MEDIUM`, advance to step 3.\n   - **Security — intra-module memory safety** (`AllocatePool`/`FreePool` pairs, `CreateEvent`/`CloseEvent`, `OpenProtocol`/`CloseProtocol` within the same module): `grep_search` across the module directory for the complementary operation on the same pointer, GUID, or handle (same procedure as the Lifecycle sub-rule below). **NULL dereference FP guard:** for a missing NULL check on a parameter or return value, additionally scan all call sites of the enclosing function — if every reachable call path guarantees a non-NULL value, close as `FALSE POSITIVE` and tag `[NULL-DEREF-CALLSITE-VERIFIED: pointer always non-NULL at dereference point]`.\n   - **Security — other intra-function** (bounds checks, flag validation, correctness issues with no cross-module consumer path): `N/A — intra-module scope`.\n   - **Lifecycle** (`AllocatePool`/`AllocatePages`, `CreateEvent`/`CreateEventEx`, `InstallProtocolInterface`, `AppendDevicePath`/`DuplicateDevicePath` with no local complementary release): `grep_search` workspace for the complementary op (`FreePool`/`FreePages`, `CloseEvent`, `UninstallProtocolInterface`) on the same pointer, GUID, or handle. **Found** → `[LIFECYCLE-PARTNER-FOUND: <file>:<line>]` → `FALSE POSITIVE` (if partner file is also in the diff, verify the partner's release paths are correct before accepting FALSE POSITIVE). **Not found** → `CONFIRMED`. **Ambiguous** (multiple unrelated matches) → `UNVERIFIED`.\n   - **ELINK**: `grep_search` for the registered function definition; compare its signature to the ELINK cache prototype. Mismatch → `CONFIRMED`. Cache entry `[NOT FOUND]` → `UNVERIFIED — [ELINK-PROTOTYPE-UNVERIFIED: manual build verification required]`.\n   - **VFR `efivarstore` lock**: `grep_search` workspace for `RequestToLock` with matching variable name or GUID. Found → `FALSE POSITIVE`. Not found → `CONFIRMED`.\n   - **ASL/FDF**: classify as Security if the finding involves an FV boundary, SMRAM region, MMRAM region, or the file path contains `Smm`/`StandaloneMm`/`SecureBoot`/`Auth` — apply Security sub-rule. Otherwise → `N/A — intra-module scope`.\n   - **All other non-security**: `N/A — intra-module scope`.\n   - **Gate after Step 2:** If search results are incomplete, ambiguous, or timed out, continue to Step 3 with `Confidence: MEDIUM` unless Step 1 already resolved the finding.\n3. **Spec determination** — choose exactly one verdict:\n   - `CONFIRMED {spec: <spec> §X.Y.Z}` — normatively prohibited.\n   - `FALSE POSITIVE — <reason>` — permitted or valid for MODULE_TYPE. Increment `FP: N`. If the finding was upgraded via a normative SHALL, record `[SHALL-UPGRADE-SUPPRESSED: <reason>]` and revert severity to the pre-upgrade level.\n   - `⚠️ UNVERIFIED — manual check recommended` — `Confidence: MEDIUM`. Do NOT upgrade severity.\n\n\n##### IDV-Lite for MINOR-A:\n1. Context read — confirm the changed code and local surrounding logic were read.\n2. Spec determination — cite the relevant spec or project rule and classify as `CONFIRMED`, `FALSE POSITIVE`, or `UNVERIFIED`.\n3. Escalate to full IDV only when the finding crosses a trust boundary, depends on ownership outside the current module, or cannot be resolved from local context.\n\n##### Lite REVIEW_PATH IDV Scope: Step 2 = same-file callers only (`.c`/`.h`), or same-package `grep_search` for consumers of the changed SDL token / ELINK / INF section (non-`.c`/`.h` files). Lifecycle Partner Search still applies. Use full IDV for CRITICAL/MAJOR; IDV-Lite for MINOR-A unless a boundary-crossing condition forces escalation.\n##### Scaling for Large Reviews (25+ Findings): Group findings by module (same `.c`/`.h` file or same package). Within each group: Step 1 (context read) = read the enclosing function body **once**, shared across all findings in that function; Step 2 (cross-module scope) = run one `deep-search` per unique protocol GUID or lifecycle symbol, shared across all findings citing that GUID/symbol; Step 3 (spec determination) = individual verdict **per finding** — never share verdicts across findings. Record the shared read/search result once and reference it by note in each finding's IDV block (e.g., `\"shared search — see F<N> IDV Step 2\"`).\n\n**Stage 2 checkpoint state** is maintained via the per-file flush to `Detailed_Review_Report.md` and per-file `cc_registry.md` Review Status updates. No separate `s2_checkpoint.md` file is required or written. Crash recovery uses `cc_registry.md` Review Status = `NA` as the resume pointer (see Interrupt Recovery).\n\n### Step 2.2 — Cross-File Consistency\n\n**GUID uniqueness check:** Cross-reference any new GUID literal definitions (i.e., `+` hunk lines matching `{ 0x[0-9a-fA-F]` pattern) in the diff against all workspace `.dec` files using `grep_search`. A collision where the same GUID value is registered under two different names → CRITICAL. Skip and mark `[GUID-CHECK: SKIPPED — no new GUID literals in diff]` when no such lines exist.\n\n- Macro consistency (same `#define`, different values → MAJOR)\n- Cross-module ABI: struct changes → verify field offsets preserved or consumers updated, `sizeof()` assumptions hold\n- Protocol struct changes: function pointer reorder → CRITICAL unless GUID changed\n- Copyright: note if 3+ files share same violation\n\n**Cross-file finding attribution:** Findings from this step are written to a dedicated **`## Cross-File Findings`** section in `Detailed_Review_Report.md`, placed after all per-file sections. Each finding must list all implicated files. Finding IDs continue sequentially from the last per-file `F<N>`. When multiple files are implicated, pin the finding to the highest-priority file (P1 > P2 > P3) for verdict scoring.\n\n### Step 2.3 — Stage 2 Gate\n\n**All must pass:**\n- All files processed (Agent State `FILE: #<total>/<total>` reached)\n- **No P1 file skipped** — files in P1 (SMM/SMRAM/StandaloneMM/MMRAM/SecureBoot/Crypto) must be fully reviewed with all CCs recorded; a single skipped P1 file unconditionally fails this gate\n- Skipped files ≤ 10% of total non-binary, non-excluded files\n- All CC entries reviewed and status recorded in context memory (no `[PENDING]` CC entries)\n- All changed hunks read, all function bodies read\n\nCoverage: `| Hunks: total/reviewed/skipped | CCs: total/reviewed |`\n\n**After gate passes:** All per-file finding sections must have been flushed to `Detailed_Review_Report.md` and all CC Review Status values must have been updated in `cc_registry.md`. **Must** verify `cc_registry.md` has no remaining `NA` Review Status entries (other than `EXCLUDED` CCs) — any remaining `NA` entries **must** cause a return to Stage 2 for those CCs before Stage 3 begins. Stage 3 reads findings from `Detailed_Review_Report.md` and CC statuses from `cc_registry.md` directly — context memory need only hold running Agent State totals and INF-DELTA reachability notes.\n\n---\n\n## Stage 3: Decision\n\n> Scope: Verify per-file sections in `Detailed_Review_Report.md`, append verdict/score/fix sections, then emit verdict. (→ Stage 3 Invariant)\n\n### Step 3.0 — Verify and Complete Detailed_Review_Report Document\n\n**Prerequisite:** **Must** verify `Detailed_Review_Report.md` exists and contains all per-file finding sections (one `## File #N:` section per non-excluded, non-skipped file). If a file section is missing, **must** resume Stage 2 for that file before proceeding. If the document does not exist at all, **must** resume Stage 2 from the first CC with `Review Status = NA` in `cc_registry.md` — the first-file flush will create the document. **Must not** proceed to Step 3.1 until this prerequisite is fully satisfied. When `RUNTIME_MODE = MEMORY-ONLY`, the prerequisite is satisfied by the equivalent content being maintained in context memory; skip the file-existence check. *Note: the verification in this step is a defensive re-check of the Stage 2 Gate (Step 2.3) — it does not constitute a second gate; no additional findings or scoring changes are made here.*\n\nThe per-file finding sections (sections 1–7 below) were written by Stage 2 per-file flushes. Stage 3 does not recreate them. Stage 3 appends only the status markers in steps 8–9, then the verdict sections in Steps 3.2–3.7.\n\n**Commit/patch header** — already in the document (written by Stage 2 first-file flush). Verify it is present; if missing, prepend it now using Stage 1 Step 1.0 data. (Stage 1 Step 1.0 data — commit SHA, author, subject, date, file counts — is sourced exclusively from context memory recorded during Stage 1; no new `read_file` or `run_in_terminal` calls are permitted here, consistent with the Stage 3 Invariant.)\n\n| Field | Commit mode source | Patch mode source |\n|-------|------------------|-------------------|\n| Review Date | Current date | Current date |\n| Author | `git show --format=\"%an <%ae>\"` | `N/A` |\n| Commit SHA | `git show --format=\"%H\"` | `N/A` |\n| Subject | `git show --format=\"%s\"` | Patch filename |\n| Files changed | Stage 1 inventory count | Stage 1 inventory count |\n\n> **Folder diff input:** Author = `Folder diff: <FOLDER_DIFF_ORG> → <FOLDER_DIFF_MOD>` · Commit SHA = `<FOLDER_DIFF_HASH>` · Subject = `<N> files: <MODIFIED> MODIFIED, <NEW> NEW, <DELETED> DELETED` · all sourced from context memory recorded in Stage 1 Step 1.0 — substitute these values for `N/A` in the above fields when input type is folder diff.\n\n**Must** verify the following sections are present in the document (already written by Stage 2). Abort Triggers (Row 1) are always HIGH confidence and are exempt from this rule.\n\n> **Row 3 vs Row 4 interaction:** Row 3 requires CONFIRMED MAJOR ≥ 3 regardless of score. Row 4 requires CONFIRMED MAJOR ≥ 1 AND Score ≥ 20. With exactly 2 CONFIRMED MAJORs on P1 files (score = 20): Row 3 does not fire — Row 4 fires (🔴 BLOCK). Each dimension is an ordered review gate evaluated sequentially.\n\n---\n\n### Dimension Applicability by File Type\n\n| Priority | File types | Applicable dimensions |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | SMM/StandaloneMM/SecureBoot/Crypto `.c`/`.h` | §1 (all triggers) · §2–§11 · §12 |\n| P2 | Standard DXE/PEI/Runtime `.c`/`.h` | §1 (all triggers) · §2–§11 · §12 |\n| P3 | `.inf`/`.dsc`/`.fdf`/`.dec` | §1 (Triggers #8, #12, #18 only) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.sdl`/`.mak`/`.cif`/`.veb` | §1 (Trigger #8 only) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.asl` | §1 (Trigger #12 if EDK2-owned) · §13 |\n| P4 | `.nasm`/`.asm` | §1 (Triggers #1, #2, #3, #15, #16 for SMM paths) · §13 |\n| P5 | `.vfr`/`.sd`/`.uni` | §13 only |\n| P6/P7 | Test/docs/scripts | §12 (copyright/`@file` only) |\n| P8 | Binary | No review (`[➡️ BINARY]`) |\n\n---\n\n### §1. Abort Trigger Gates (check FIRST)\n\nApply trigger groups in order. Skip a group if it does not apply to the current module type, file type, or changed hunk — note the skip only when it materially affected review scope. Any confirmed match produces **🛑 BLOCK** and must be recorded as `[🛑 CRITICAL – ABORT TRIGGER]`.\n\n#### Gate A — SMM Isolation and Lock-Window\n\n**Applies when:** file is SMM-related by MODULE_TYPE, path, library usage, or changed handler registration logic.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 1 | SMRAM address/pointer as return value or `OUT` param to a non-SMM caller |\n| 2 | `LocateProtocol`, `HandleProtocol`, or `gBS->` call inside an SMM handler body |\n| 3 | CommBuffer pointer or size field written back to DXE-accessible memory by an SMM handler without sanitization — return-oriented data leak |\n| 15 | SMM handler or child dispatch handle registration (`Register`, `SmmRegisterProtocolNotify`, `InstallProtocolInterface`, or `SmmInstallProtocolInterface` for child protocols such as `EFI_SMM_SW_DISPATCH2_PROTOCOL`) after `EFI_SMM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed — covers both direct handler and child-dispatch lock bypass |\n| 16 | `AllocatePages` for SMRAM-resident code without configuring NX attributes via `EFI_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES_PROTOCOL` — leaves SMM code pages executable, enabling code-injection if SMRAM is writable |\n\n#### Gate A-MM — Standalone MM Isolation\n\n**Applies when:** MODULE_TYPE = `MM_STANDALONE` or `MM_CORE_STANDALONE` or path contains `StandaloneMm/`, `MmStandalone/`, or `Standalone/`.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| MM-1 | `gSmst->` (traditional SMM services table) used inside a Standalone MM module — must use `gMmst->` (`EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE`) instead; direct `gSmst->` access from `MM_STANDALONE` is an architectural violation = CRITICAL |\n| MM-2 | `EFI_MM_COMMUNICATE` CommBuffer dereferenced using `SmmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` instead of `MmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` — wrong header struct for Standalone MM path = MAJOR |\n| MM-3 | MM handler or child dispatch handle registered after `EFI_MM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed — same lock-window violation as Trigger #15, applied to Standalone MM context = CRITICAL |\n| MM-4 | `gBS->` or any Boot Services pointer accessed inside a Standalone MM handler — Boot Services are unavailable in Standalone MM execution context = CRITICAL |\n| MM-5 | `AllocatePages` for MMRAM-resident code without configuring NX attributes via `EFI_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTES_PROTOCOL` — leaves MM code pages executable, enabling code-injection if MMRAM is writable = CRITICAL |\n| MM-6 | `gMmst->MmLocateProtocol()` or `gMmst->MmHandleProtocol()` output pointer dereferenced without first verifying return is `EFI_SUCCESS` — null-protocol dereference inside Standalone MM handler = MAJOR |\n\n> **Gate A vs Gate A-MM:** Apply Gate A for `DXE_SMM_DRIVER`/`SMM_CORE`. Apply Gate A-MM for `MM_STANDALONE`/`MM_CORE_STANDALONE`. When MODULE_TYPE is unresolved and both SMM and Standalone MM are plausible, apply both gates and record `[DUAL-GATE-APPLIED: A + A-MM — MODULE_TYPE unresolved]`. When dual-gate fires produce overlapping findings on the **same line**, merge into a single finding citing both violations: `[DUAL-GATE: Gate A Trigger #N + Gate A-MM Trigger MM-N]`; severity is CRITICAL regardless. Do not emit two separate findings for the same line. **A dual-gate merged finding counts as ONE CRITICAL for Agent State, scoring, and verdict Rows 2–4 regardless of how many triggers contributed.**\n\n#### Gate B — CommBuffer and Untrusted-Size\n\n**Applies when:** changed code reads CommBuffer fields, dispatch contexts, DMA buffers, or untrusted size arithmetic.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 4 | `CopyMem`/`SetMem`/array write where length comes from external input with no bounds check |\n| 5 | CommBuffer, DMA buffer, or dispatch pointer dereferenced before size/NULL check |\n| 6 | CommBuffer cast or field-index without `≥ sizeof` guard — **(a)** SW SMI handler casts `DispatchContext`/CommBuffer without checking `MessageLength ≥ sizeof(struct)`; **(b)** `SmmCommunicateHeader.MessageLength` used to cast or index CommBuffer without a `≥ sizeof` guard — apply whichever sub-point matches; never fire both on the same line |\n| 11 | `+`/`*`/`<<` on untrusted values fed to `CopyMem`/`SetMem`/`AllocatePool` size without SafeIntLib |\n| 17 | SMM handler reads CommBuffer fields a second time after initial validation instead of using an SMRAM-local copy — CommBuffer must be copied to an SMRAM-local struct before any code path that performs a **functional** field access (i.e., any access that influences control flow, output, or memory operations); non-functional reads inside `DEBUG()` macros are exempt when the module is not built with debug output in the release configuration; any subsequent functional field access that reads from the original DXE-accessible pointer is a TOCTOU exploit |\n\n> **Overlap note — CommBuffer family (#5, #6, #17):** Apply the most specific trigger only; never stack multiple triggers on the same line:\n> - **#5** — pointer/size dereferenced *before* any NULL/size check\n> - **#6** — cast or indexed without `≥ sizeof` guard\n> - **#17** — re-reads CommBuffer fields after validation instead of using the SMRAM-local copy\n\n#### Gate C — Runtime, S3, and Authenticated-Variable\n\n**Applies when:** changed code touches runtime callbacks, S3 boot script logic, or security database variables.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 7 | `gBS->` call inside `ExitBootServices` callback or `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` after `SetVirtualAddressMap`. **Also flag** `FreePool()`, `FreePages()`, or `FreeBuffer()` (MemoryAllocationLib wrappers or direct `gBS->` form) called inside an `ExitBootServices` callback — Boot Services memory management is unavailable at this point; calling these APIs causes unpredictable exceptions — CRITICAL. Detection: function registered via `CreateEventEx()` with `gEfiEventExitBootServicesGuid` or `CreateEvent(EVT_SIGNAL_EXIT_BOOT_SERVICES, ...)` whose body contains `FreePool`, `FreePages`, or `FreeBuffer` |\n| 10 | `EFI_S3_SAVE_STATE_PROTOCOL.Write()` called after `EndOfDxe`, or target region writable by DXE |\n| 13 | `SetVariable` to `db`/`dbx`/`dbt` (`EFI_IMAGE_SECURITY_DATABASE*`) without `EFI_VARIABLE_TIME_BASED_AUTHENTICATED_WRITE_ACCESS` attribute — bypasses image security database authentication |\n| 14 | `EFI_S3_SAVE_STATE_PROTOCOL` callback registration or `.Write()` call inside a `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` or after `SmmReadyToLock` notification — S3 boot-script window violation |\n\n#### Gate D — Build, Ownership, and Image-Policy\n\n**Applies when:** patch changes SDL/build configuration, upstream-owned code, or image verification flow.\n\n| # | What to look for |\n|---|------------------|\n| 8 | `KEYS_DIR` or `DEBUG_MODE` token patched — follow chain to confirm the unsafe state: test keys still enabled in a release build (`DEBUG_MODE = 0`) |\n| 9 | Image verification returns `EFI_SUCCESS` unconditionally or skips signature check |\n| 12 | File under `Intel/`, `MdePkg/`, `MdeModulePkg/`, `SecurityPkg/`, `CryptoPkg/`, `StandaloneMmPkg/`, or `UefiCpuPkg/` modified without an AMI OVERRIDE marker. **Accepted syntax (any of the following is valid — do NOT fire if any variant is present):** For `.c`/`.h`: (1) `// AMI OVERRIDE START/END`, (2) `//APTIOV_OVERRIDE_START/END`, (3) `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:/END:`, (4) `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_START:/END:`, (5) any `//` comment matching regex `(AMI\\|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*START`. For `.inf`/`.dec`/`.dsc`/`.fdf`/`.mak`/`.cif`: same patterns with `#` comment prefix. Fire **only** when the changed hunk contains **no** override marker of any accepted variant. **AMI copyright banner exemption:** When a file is classified as ⚙️ **Third-party with AMI overrides** (file contains BOTH third-party and AMI copyright), the AMI copyright block itself (lines matching `Copyright.*AMI` or `//***` banner pattern) does NOT require wrapping in override markers — do NOT fire Trigger #12 for a hunk consisting solely of AMI copyright banner lines, provided at least one correctly-formed override block exists elsewhere in the same file. If the AMI copyright banner is the ONLY change in the file with no override markers anywhere → fire Trigger #12 (copyright-only change with zero markers = stealth modification). |\n| 18 | `InstallProtocolInterface` or `InstallMultipleProtocolInterfaces` targeting `gEfiSecurityArchProtocolGuid` or `gEfiSecurity2ArchProtocolGuid` in a `DXE_DRIVER` outside `SecurityPkg/`. Exception: designated security handlers in `SecurityPkg/` or `AmiSecureBootPkg/` are exempt |\n\n**On match:** mark `[🛑 CRITICAL – ABORT TRIGGER]` and continue reviewing remaining CCs.\n\n**Trigger #8 evaluation chain:** (1) patched value → (2) project `.sdl` → (3) `CrbPkg/*.sdl` → (4) `AmiPkg/Configuration/Configuration.sdl`. Fire only when the unsafe combination is confirmed: test keys selected while `DEBUG_MODE = 0` (release build). If PCD cache marks the token `[BUILD-TIME-ONLY]`, rely exclusively on the SDL chain walk. If also unresolvable, emit `[TRIGGER-8-UNRESOLVABLE]` as INFO — do NOT block.\n\n> Abort Triggers (#1–#18) are fully evaluated through Gates A–D. Dimensions §2–§13 must NOT re-evaluate any Abort Trigger pattern. If a dimension check overlaps with a trigger, skip it — the trigger verdict stands.\n\n---\n\n### §2. Security\n\n- `BootOrder`/`BootXXXX` NV writes without auth check = MAJOR when Secure Boot path reachable\n- New GUIDs: collision check performed in Step 2.2 mandatory GUID uniqueness check\n- Keys/passwords must not appear in `DEBUG()` args = MAJOR\n- DMA buffers in protected memory; IOMMU/VT-d enabled before DMA access — missing = CRITICAL\n- `gBS->LocateProtocol()`, `gBS->OpenProtocol()`, `gBS->HandleProtocol()` output pointer dereferenced without first verifying return is `EFI_SUCCESS` = MAJOR (null-protocol dereference)\n- `LocatePpi()`/`GetPpiList()` output pointer used without `EFI_SUCCESS` check in PEI context = MAJOR\n\n### §3. Memory Safety\n\n- **`ExitBootServices` callback — `FreePool`/`FreePages`/`FreeBuffer` forbidden:** These APIs must not be called inside an `ExitBootServices` callback (`EVT_SIGNAL_EXIT_BOOT_SERVICES` / `gEfiEventExitBootServicesGuid`). Boot Services are unavailable at this point; calling memory-free APIs causes unpredictable exceptions — CRITICAL. Memory no longer needed after boot must be freed **before** `ExitBootServices` fires. **Agent must never suggest adding `FreePool`/`FreePages`/`FreeBuffer` inside an EBS callback as a fix.** If the lifecycle check below finds a missing free whose only plausible placement is inside the EBS callback, close as `FALSE POSITIVE` — do not open a finding.\n- Every `AllocatePool`/`AllocatePages` has matching `FreePool`/`FreePages` on all exit paths — missing = MAJOR. **EBS exception:** if the only location where the free is absent is an `ExitBootServices` callback body, treat as `FALSE POSITIVE` per rule above — never suggest adding the free call there.\n- No use-after-free, no dangling pointers, no protocol pointers held across uninstall — violation = CRITICAL\n- **`CR()`/`BASE_CR()` macro cast without Signature guard** — cast recovering outer struct via `CR()`/`BASE_CR()` must verify `Struct->Signature == EXPECTED_SIGNATURE` immediately before or after the macro; missing guard = MAJOR when the pointer is externally supplied or crosses a trust boundary (e.g., originating from a protocol caller, CommBuffer, or DXE↔SMM interface); missing guard = MINOR-A when the pointer originates from the module's own protocol installation and no external attacker path exists; if SMM-resident struct with DXE-accessible pointer origin = CRITICAL\n- No unsafe string APIs (`StrCpy`/`AsciiStrCpy`/`sprintf`) — use safe `*S` equivalents = MAJOR\n- `AsciiSPrint`/`UnicodeSPrint`/`AsciiVSPrint`/`UnicodeVSPrint`: `BufferSize` from untrusted arithmetic without SafeIntLib = MAJOR\n- Credential/key buffers zeroed with `ZeroMem` before `FreePool` — missing = MAJOR if buffer held password, key, or auth token\n- Local stack arrays > 4 KB in SMM or Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`) = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` return checked `EFI_SUCCESS` before arithmetic on `DataSize` — using `DataSize` after failure = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` two-pass size pattern: verify (a) `DataSize > 0` before allocation and (b) second call returns `EFI_SUCCESS` before buffer dereference — either missing = MAJOR. *Cross-check:* if the variable is security-sensitive, also verify §4 `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` is present\n- **API migration — double pointer OUT parameters:** When `AllocatePool`/`AllocateZeroPool`/`AllocatePages`/`AllocateRuntimePool` replaces `gBS->AllocatePool(Type, Size, &Buffer)`, verify correct dereference: `VOID **OutputParam` → must write `*OutputParam = AllocatePool(...)` and check `*OutputParam == NULL`. Assigning to the local parameter copy leaves the caller's pointer unchanged = CRITICAL (memory leak + uninitialized pointer dereference)\n- **API migration — mixed allocation/deallocation APIs:** MemoryAllocationLib allocation paired with `gBS->FreePool`/`gBS->FreePages` = MAJOR. Correct pairings: MemoryAllocationLib → `FreePool`/`FreePages`; Boot Services → `gBS->FreePool`/`gBS->FreePages`. Partial migration in progress → flag as MAJOR with recommendation to complete consistently\n- **String pointer storage in struct members:** Struct members of type `CHAR8 *`, `CHAR16 *`, or `char *` assigned from allocated buffers must either (a) copy the string data with `AllocateCopyPool`/`AllocateZeroPool` + `AsciiStrCpyS`/`StrCpyS` or (b) transfer ownership by nulling the source pointer after assignment. Pattern: `Context->StringPtr = AllocatedBuffer; FreePool(AllocatedBuffer);` without prior copy = CRITICAL (dangling pointer). Correct patterns: (1) `Context->StringPtr = AllocateCopyPool(AsciiStrSize(Src), Src); FreePool(Src);` or (2) `Context->StringPtr = Src; Src = NULL;` (ownership transfer). Verify the stored pointer is freed in the struct's cleanup/destructor function; missing cleanup = MAJOR (memory leak)\n- **String pointer array cleanup:** For arrays like `CHAR8 *StringSet[]` or `CHAR16 *StringArray[]`, ownership must be explicit. If strings are heap-allocated copies (via `AllocateCopyPool`, `AllocatePool` + `StrCpyS`, or `StrDuplicate`-like helpers), each element must be freed individually in a loop before freeing the array itself: `for (i = 0; i < Count; i++) { FreePool(StringArray[i]); } FreePool(StringArray);` — missing per-element free = MAJOR (memory leak). If strings are borrowed references (pointers to static strings, .rodata, or external buffers not owned by this module), freeing individual elements = CRITICAL (use-after-free / double-free). Detection heuristic: trace string assignment origin — if from `AllocatePool`/`AllocateCopyPool`/`StrDuplicate`, ownership transferred; if from string literal, global buffer, or function returning `CONST CHAR*`, borrowed reference. Ambiguous cases → `Confidence: MEDIUM` with recommendation to document ownership contract\n\n### §4. Variable Service Security\n\n- Security-sensitive NV variables locked via `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` before `EndOfDxe` — missing = MAJOR\n- `GetVariable()` single-call with hardcoded buffer on untrusted variable = MAJOR (two-pass pattern → §3)\n- `EFI_VARIABLE_AUTHENTICATION_2`: `AuthInfo.Hdr.wCertificateType` must be `WIN_CERT_TYPE_EFI_GUID` — writing without valid descriptor = MAJOR\n- `EFI_VARIABLE_NON_VOLATILE + RUNTIME_ACCESS` audited for necessity; large NV write without `QueryVariableInfo` = MINOR\n\n### §5. S3 Resume Security\n\n- Pointers passed to `Write()` must not be stack variables or DXE-writable ACPI NVS buffers — violation = MAJOR\n- Hardware writes to TSEG/SMRR registers must be immediately followed by a lock step — missing = MAJOR\n\n### §6. Concurrency & Locking\n\n- `EFI_LOCK`: `EfiInitializeLock` before first use; every `EfiAcquireLock` has matching `EfiReleaseLock` — missing release = MAJOR\n- SMM: `SmmAcquireLock`/`SmmReleaseLock` around shared globals from multiple CPUs/APs — unprotected = MAJOR\n- Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`): `SmmAcquireLock`/`SmmReleaseLock` are not available; use `EFI_SPIN_LOCK` (via `SynchronizationLib`) to protect shared globals accessed by MM handlers from multiple APs — unprotected `= MAJOR`\n- `EFI_SPIN_LOCK`: `InitializeSpinLock` before use; `AcquireSpinLock`/`ReleaseSpinLock` balanced — unbalanced = MAJOR\n- TPL: raising to lower TPL than current = MAJOR; `TPL_HIGH_LEVEL` outside interrupt context = MAJOR\n- `EFI_MM_MP_PROTOCOL.DispatchProcedure()`: shared globals from AP procedures must be guarded by `EFI_SPIN_LOCK` — unprotected = MAJOR (PI 1.8 §4.10.2)\n\n### §7. Spec Compliance (UEFI 2.10+ / PI 1.8+)\n\n- `[UEFI]` UEFI types only (`EFI_STATUS`, `UINTN`, `UINT8/16/32/64`, `BOOLEAN`, `VOID`, `EFI_HANDLE`) — no `int`/`char`/`void` = MINOR\n- `[UEFI]` `gRT->` callable post-`ExitBootServices` — runtime-safe memory only = MAJOR\n- `[UEFI]` Protocols installed/uninstalled properly (pointer lifetime → §3)\n- `[UEFI]` Variable services: proper attributes, size validated, GUID traceable (`EFI_STATUS` checking → §8)\n- `[PI]` PEI: PPIs only, no protocols; CAR limits apply; no temp RAM pointers in HOBs\n- `[PI]` DXE: `[Depex]` lists all required protocols/GUIDs\n- `[PI]` SMM: SMRAM locked after `SmmReadyToLock`; CommBuffers validated\n- `[PI]` Standalone MM (`MM_STANDALONE`): MMRAM locked after `EFI_MM_READY_TO_LOCK_PROTOCOL` installed; CommBuffers validated using `EFI_MM_COMMUNICATE_HEADER`; `gBS->` and all Boot Services unavailable; `gSmst->` must not be used — use `gMmst->` (`EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE`) exclusively\n- `[PI]` HOBs: `GET_GUID_HOB_DATA_SIZE >= sizeof(<Type>)` validated by DXE consumers\n- `[PI]` Phase separation: PEI must not use DXE-only interfaces; runtime must not use boot-only interfaces\n\n### §8. Correctness & Lifecycle\n\n- Every `EFI_STATUS` return checked — not silently discarded = MAJOR\n- All error paths clean: no leaked resources, no held mutexes — violation = MAJOR\n- All `else`/`default` branches handle errors = MINOR — **FP guard:** before flagging, confirm the branch is not an intentional fallback path (e.g., a by-design default return or NO-OP documented in comments); if intent is by design, classify as INFO or skip\n- Re-entrancy guards for functions callable from nested events — missing = MAJOR\n- TPL safety: shared data at `TPL_APPLICATION` protected by TPL raise — unprotected = MAJOR\n- Every `CreateEvent`/`CreateEventEx` matched by `CloseEvent` on non-success paths and in `Stop()`/unload — missing = MAJOR\n- `ExitBootServices` callback must not call `gBS->`, `AllocatePool`, or `FreePool` — violation = MAJOR\n- `OpenProtocol(BY_DRIVER)` in `Start()` matched by `CloseProtocol()` in `Stop()` — mismatch = MAJOR\n- Buffers from `AppendDevicePath`/`DuplicateDevicePath` freed with `FreePool` on all exit paths — missing = MAJOR\n\n### §9. PEI-Specific Depth\n\n- Local arrays > 1 KB in any PEI function = MAJOR (CAR stack ~64–128 KB; risks overflow)\n- Pre-memory `AllocatePool` results must not be referenced after `MemoryDiscoveredPpiNotify` — stale reference = MAJOR\n- `BuildGuidDataHob` size must equal `sizeof(<struct>)` exactly — over/under = MAJOR\n- `BuildGuidDataHob` alignment: if struct natural alignment ≥ 8 bytes and `sizeof(struct)` is not a multiple, HOB data area is not naturally aligned for X64 consumer casts — undefined behavior = MAJOR\n- `GetFirstGuidHob()` result NULL-checked; `GET_GUID_HOB_DATA_SIZE` validated ≥ `sizeof(expected struct)` before cast — missing = MAJOR\n- `PeiServicesGetBootMode()` consulted before S3/recovery-specific init = MINOR\n\n### §10. Capsule / FMP Security\n\n- `LowestSupportedImageVersion` honored; any bypass = CRITICAL (anti-rollback)\n- `CheckImage()` return gated before `SetImage()` — `SetImage()` without prior success = MAJOR\n- `UpdateImageTypeId` matched against `GetImageInfo()` `ImageTypeId` — silent mismatch = MAJOR\n- Capsule payload size validated against actual buffer length before parsing — missing = MAJOR\n- `CAPSULE_FLAGS_PERSIST_ACROSS_RESET` set only when reset is required — otherwise = MINOR\n\n### §11. General Algorithmic & Functional Logic\n\nReview functional correctness of changed `.c`/`.h` code independent of UEFI/PI spec mandates. Apply Pre-Finding Gate before opening any finding. Findings here are typically MINOR unless they cause data corruption or incorrect control flow affecting firmware reliability. Tag findings `[LOGIC]`.\n\n> **§8 / §11 tie-breaker:** If a correctness issue also involves `EFI_STATUS` semantics, protocol lifetime, event/lock balance, or resource lifecycle, classify it under §8 (Correctness & Lifecycle) and do not duplicate it under §11.\n\n- **Off-by-one errors:** Loop bounds (`<` vs `<=`), buffer index, array sizing — incorrect bound = MAJOR if buffer accessed\n- **Inverted or wrong condition:** `==` vs `!=`, `>` vs `>=`, negated flag, wrong enum in `switch`/`if` — causes incorrect branch = MAJOR\n- **Dead / unreachable code:** `return`/`break`/unconditional assignment renders subsequent lines unreachable — MINOR; if it masks error path = MAJOR — **FP guard:** an explicit early-return guard (e.g., `if (Ptr == NULL) { return EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER; }`) or a documented intentional fallback is not dead code; do NOT flag it even if the happy path always executes after it\n- **Stale or wrong variable used:** Copy-paste error with wrong variable — MAJOR if data corruption results\n- **Incorrect bit manipulation:** Wrong shift, missing mask, bit cleared instead of set — MAJOR if affects hardware register or security flag; MINOR otherwise\n- **State machine correctness:** Missing transition, unreachable terminal state, skipped required intermediate — MAJOR if firmware stalls or mis-sequences init\n- **Integer wrap / truncation (non-security):** Narrowing cast or decrement below zero on `UINTN`/`UINT32` — MINOR if no security path; MAJOR if controls allocation or copy\n- **Redundant or contradictory logic:** Condition always true/false, duplicate `if` branches — MINOR\n- **Incorrect return value:** Returns value not matching documented contract — MAJOR\n- **Uninitialized variable used:** Local variable read before assignment on some code path — MAJOR if influences control flow or output\n- **Algorithm correctness:** Sorting/searching/checksum/table-walk loops: verify algorithm matches stated intent — MAJOR if incorrect result silently propagates\n- **Preprocessor conditional scope violation:** A variable, label, or function *defined* inside an `#if`/`#ifdef`/`#ifndef` block but *referenced* outside the enclosing `#endif` — causes a compilation error when the condition is not met = MAJOR `[LOGIC]`. Detection: when a diff hunk introduces a symbol definition inside a conditional block, `grep_search` the file for uses of that symbol name outside the enclosing `#if`/`#endif` pair; if found → MAJOR. **FP guard:** if the same symbol is also declared or defined unconditionally elsewhere in the file (e.g., a guard-free fallback declaration), do NOT flag.\n\n### §12. EDK II C Coding Standard 2.2+\n\n- **Naming:** PascalCase functions · `g` prefix globals · ALL_CAPS macros/constants = MINOR\n- **Indentation:** 2 spaces per level; no tabs = MINOR\n- **Comments:** Doxygen `/** ... **/` for file/function docs; `//` inline = MINOR\n- **No implicit fall-through** in `switch` — end each `case` with `break`, `return`, or `// FALL THROUGH` = MINOR; if it masks a security branch = MAJOR\n- **Magic numbers:** named `#define` macros only = MINOR\n- **ASSERT:** via `DebugLib`; never sole security gate (stripped by `MDEPKG_NDEBUG`) = MAJOR. A **sole security gate** means `ASSERT()` is the only check preventing an unsafe operation — e.g., `ASSERT(Buffer != NULL)` immediately before `CopyMem(Dst, Buffer, Size)` with no prior `if (Buffer == NULL) return;` runtime guard. ASSERTs protecting internal invariants structurally unreachable from external attacker-controlled input are not security gates; classify those as INFO.\n- **Parameter qualifiers:** `CONST`/`IN`/`OUT`/`IN OUT` match actual usage; `IN` param must not be modified = MINOR\n- **Copyright year** ≥ commit year; `@file` block present = INFO\n- **Include order:** `<Uefi.h>` or `<Pei.h>` first, then `<Token.h>`, AMI libs, EDK2 libs, protocols, platform headers = INFO\n- **Code Organization & Placement** — review only high-signal structural cases. Aggregate into single `[🔷 MINOR-B]` finding tagged `[CODE-ORG-AGGREGATE]`:\n   - Function prototypes/declarations mid-file (after first `{`) = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - `#include` directives not at file top (after `#define`/`typedef`/`struct`/`extern`/function body) = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - Global variable declarations after first function definition = MINOR `[CODE-ORG]`\n   - All other placement issues: better handled by linting/CI unless they hide a security guard or cause build error\n- **INF section rules:** see §13 for `[Packages]` ordering, section validation, and DSC cross-check\n\n### §13. File-Type Specific (non-`.c`/`.h` files only)\n\n#### `.inf` files\n\n- `[Defines]` complete · `[Sources]` lists changed files · `[Packages]` MdePkg first\n- `[LibraryClasses]`/`[Protocols]`/`[Ppis]`/`[Guids]` match actual usage (cross-check DSC) — **FP guard for section classification:** before flagging a GUID identifier as in the wrong section, read the owning package `.dec` file to confirm its declaration section (`[Protocols]`, `[Ppis]`, or `[Guids]`); the INF section must match the `.dec` declaration — do NOT rely on naming conventions alone; if `.dec` is inaccessible, tag `[INF-SECTION-UNVERIFIED]` and downgrade to INFO\n- `[Depex]` covers all required protocols and notify-install callbacks\n- `[Pcd]`/`[PcdEx]` entries match actual usage — before flagging an entry as unused, apply the two-step check:\n  - Step 1: grep the module's `.c` source for `PcdGet*()`/`PcdSet*()` on that PCD name\n  - Step 2: if Step 1 returns no matches, **grep the headers transitively included by the module** for `_PCD_VALUE_<PcdName>` or `_PCD_SIZE_<PcdName>` — EDK2 emits these as compile-time array-dimension constants into `AutoGen.h` only when the PCD is declared in `[Pcd]`; a header expression such as `UINT32 Table[_PCD_VALUE_PcdFoo]` is a valid passive consumer that mandates the `[Pcd]` entry\n  - If Step 2 finds a match → `FALSE POSITIVE`; do NOT open a finding. Only flag unused when **both** steps return no matches.\n- INF-DELTA mismatches from Stage 1 cache: apply the three-tier severity as defined in Step 3.1.7 (CRITICAL → security-critical; MAJOR → default; MINOR → call path unreachable)\n\n#### `.sdl` files\n\n> 📖 **SDL skill — load on demand only:** When `SDL-TOKEN`, `SDL-ELINK`, `SDL-MODULE`, `SDL-PCDMAP`, or `SDL-LIBMAP` CCs are present in the Stage 1 registry, load the `/sdl-handling` skill (`.github/skills/sdl-handling/SKILL.md`) for authoritative Aptio V field names, syntax rules, validation checks, and DSC/FDF translation tables. **Do not load this skill when no SDL CCs are registered — it is not needed and increases review time unnecessarily.**\n\n**Authoritative Aptio V field names (skill is the source of truth — these override the SDL spec document names):**\n\n| Object | Correct field name in Aptio V SDL | Spec-doc alias — appears only in NDA field tables, NOT in real SDL; do NOT require this name in submitted code and do NOT flag submitted code that uses the correct left-column name |\n|--------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `INFComponent` | `ModuleTypes` (plural) | `Module_Type` |\n| `LIBRARYMAPPING` | `ModuleTypes` (plural) | `Module_Type` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `GuidSpace` | `Guid` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `PcdType` (full `\"Pcds\"` prefix required) | `Pcd_Type` |\n| `PcdMapping` | `DataType` | `Data_Type` |\n| `FFS_FILE` | `Apriori_Index` must be a quoted string | bare integer |\n\n**False positive guards — do NOT open findings for these valid Aptio V SDL patterns:**\n\n| Pattern observed | Correct interpretation — not a defect |\n|-----------------|---------------------------------------|\n| Multiple `Token = \"A\" \"=\" \"1\"` lines on one SDL object | AND-logic multi-condition — not a duplicate field violation |\n| Two `PcdMapping` blocks sharing the same `Name` but inverse `Token` conditions | Valid else-branch pattern — not a TOKEN uniqueness or duplicate-block violation |\n| `FFS_FILE` block with no `Module_Type` field | `Module_Type` is **mutually exclusive** with `INFComponent`, `File_Stmt`, and `OpRom` per NDA spec — when `INFComponent` is present (normal Aptio V case), `Module_Type` must be absent; do NOT flag this absence as a missing required field |\n| `LIBRARYMAPPING` `Instance = \"Pkg.ComponentName\"` dot format | Required format — not a path error |\n\n- TOKEN uniqueness and correct override layer · PcdMapping type/guards correct · MODULE path valid · `INFComponent.Name` unique across all SDL files · `INFComponent.File` path relative to Package root\n- LibraryMapping `Class` / `Instance` (`\"Package.ComponentName\"` dot format) / `ModuleTypes` correct\n- ELINK: no duplicate Name+Parent; missing trailing comma on function-name entry = MAJOR (hard build error); verify return type + param types against cached prototype\n  - Confirmed signature mismatch = MAJOR; escalate to CRITICAL when hook runs in security-boundary-sensitive path — determined by chain name keywords (`Smm`/`StandaloneMm`/`SecureBoot`/`Auth`/`Capsule`) **or** registered function's MODULE_TYPE being `DXE_SMM_DRIVER`, `SMM_CORE`, `MM_STANDALONE`, `MM_CORE_STANDALONE`, `DXE_RUNTIME_DRIVER` or similar\n  - `VOID*`↔typed-pointer = MAJOR\n  - Typedef not found = MINOR — `[ELINK-PROTOTYPE-UNVERIFIED: manual build verification required]`\n- `DISABLE_CAPSULE_AUTHENTICATION=1` = MAJOR · `SDL_REGRESSION` entries = MAJOR\n- For `KEYS_DIR` / `DEBUG_MODE` TOKEN changes: apply Trigger #8 (§1 Gate D)\n- Security-sensitive ELINK chains: verify hook does not bypass upstream security\n- **TOKEN rename or removal — consumer dependency check:** When a diff deletes a `TOKEN` block or changes a TOKEN `Name` field, extract the old name from the removed diff lines (`-    Name  = \"OLD_TOKEN_NAME\"`). Run `grep_search` workspace-wide across `.c`, `.h`, `.sdl`, `.mak`, and `.asl` files for the old token name. Consumers to detect: `#if OLD_TOKEN_NAME`, `#ifdef OLD_TOKEN_NAME`, `defined(OLD_TOKEN_NAME)`, `$(OLD_TOKEN_NAME)` in `.mak`/`.sdl` `Value` fields, `Token = \"OLD_TOKEN_NAME\"` SDL conditions. **Any match = MAJOR** — the old name is still consumed; a rename without a global update causes consumers to silently evaluate to `0` (undefined macro = 0 in the C preprocessor) or fail SDL dependency resolution with no compile error, making it a silent behavioral regression. No consumers found → PASS. Tag `[TOKEN-DEPENDENCY: <N> consumer(s) found — <file:line list>]` or `[TOKEN-DEPENDENCY: CLEAR — no consumers of old name detected]`.\n- **ELINK chain-root rename or removal — orphan child check:** When a diff deletes or renames an ELINK that has no `Parent` field (`InvokeOrder = ReplaceParent` — a chain root), extract the old `Name` value. Run `grep_search` in `.sdl` files for `Parent  = \"<old-name>\"`. Also check `.c` files for the old generated macro name (typically `<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE_OF_NAME>` used in `extern` or array declarations). **Any match = MAJOR** — child ELINK entries point to a non-existent root; the SDL build tool generates an empty or broken dispatch list, silently dropping all registered hooks. Tag `[ELINK-ROOT-ORPHAN: <N> child(ren) still reference old root \"<old-name>\"]`.\n- **ELINK leaf-entry removal — hook removal check:** When a diff removes an ELINK that has a `Parent` field (a leaf/contributor entry registering a function into a chain), verify the removed hook is not the sole registered entry for a security-sensitive chain (keywords in chain name: `Smm`, `StandaloneMm`, `SecureBoot`, `Auth`, `Capsule`, `Password`, `Key`). Sole security hook removed → **MAJOR**. Non-security or non-sole hook removed → **MINOR-A**. Tag `[ELINK-HOOK-REMOVED: <function-name> unregistered from chain \"<parent-name>\"]`.\n\n#### `.dec` files\n\n- `[Defines]` complete · `[Includes]` paths valid · GUID/PCD entries unique = MAJOR\n\n#### `.fdf` files\n\n- FV names match DSC · no region overlap · `AmiTrustedFvPkg` boundaries intact · security modules in correct FV\n- Boundary or security-module violation = CRITICAL; other = MAJOR\n\n#### `.vfr`/`.sd`/`.uni` files\n\n- Varstore type/size matches C struct · Question IDs unique = MAJOR · INTERACTIVE+callback pairing correct = MAJOR\n- No orphaned `suppressif` · Security options not inadvertently hidden = MAJOR · String tokens present in `.uni` = MINOR\n- `efivarstore` binding: verify `VariableLock->RequestToLock()` exists before `EndOfDxe` — missing lock = MAJOR when the variable carries `RUNTIME_ACCESS` attribute or contains security-sensitive data (boot order, auth tokens, keys); missing lock = MINOR-A when the variable lacks `RUNTIME_ACCESS` and is a non-security HII staging buffer whose writes are confined to the boot-services phase; verify backing variable uses `EFI_VARIABLE_NON_VOLATILE` — volatile-backed varstore silently loses data on warm reset = MAJOR\n\n#### `.asl` files\n\n- `_STA` bits 5–31 not set = MINOR\n- `OperationRegion` field access width matches field alignment — mismatch = MAJOR\n- `_OSC` input `Buffer` ≥ 16 bytes; undersized dereference = MAJOR\n- `Notify()` opcode validated for device type; out-of-range = MINOR\n- `_PRS` end-tag present; `_CRS` buffer size consistent with descriptor list — truncated = MAJOR\n- No hardcoded MMIO/PCI addresses conflicting with bridge `_CRS` or DRHD entries = MAJOR\n- `_DSM` implementation: `Arg2` (function index) range-checked before dispatch; `Arg3` (function-argument package) structure validated before element access — missing validation = MAJOR; `Arg0` (UUID buffer) matched against the expected GUID before any `_DSM` handler is invoked — missing UUID check allows wrong-handler invocation = MAJOR\n- `OperationRegion` field `AccessType` must be compatible with the field's `BitOffset` and `BitLength` — e.g., `ByteAcc` field with `BitOffset` not on an 8-bit boundary, or `WordAcc` without 16-bit alignment = MAJOR\n- `Notify()` target device must be defined and reachable within the current ASL namespace scope — referencing an undefined or out-of-scope device node = MAJOR\n\n#### `.nasm`/`.asm` files\n\n- Stack alignment preserved per x64/IA32 calling convention (16-byte for x64, 4-byte for IA32) — misalignment = MAJOR\n- Callee-saved registers (RBX, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15) preserved across function calls — missing preservation = MAJOR\n- For SMM entry/handler code (`SmiEntry`, `SmiException`, `*Smm*.nasm`): no `gBS->` or Boot Services calls — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #2); SMRAM pointers not leaked to non-SMM code — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #1); handler registered after `ReadyToLock` — CRITICAL (§1 Trigger #15)\n- Control-flow integrity: RET instructions paired with CALL; no arbitrary JMP to computed addresses without validation — unpaired = MAJOR\n- Interrupt flag (`CLI`/`STI`) manipulation justified and paired — unbalanced = MAJOR for SMM/exception handlers\n- Memory operand sizes match declared data types — size mismatch = MAJOR\n- CET (Control-flow Enforcement Technology) compliance when `CET_ENABLED`: shadow stack operations correct; ENDBR64/ENDBR32 present at indirect call targets — missing = MINOR when CET disabled; MAJOR when CET enabled per INF `[Defines]` or build flags\n- For S3 resume code: temporary stack usage bounds-checked; no persistent pointers to CAR/temp memory stored in HOBs or variables — unbounded stack = MAJOR\n\n#### `.veb` files\n\nThe `.veb` file is the project manifest that maps every `.cif` component to its source-control label. Each entry has the format:\n`\"<path>.cif\"= \"SS: AptioV;$/<source-path>;<ModuleName>_<LabelNumber>\"`\nThe label is the last `;`-delimited token. Multiple `.cif` entries for the same module share the same label. Skip any entry whose value is `Private`.\n\n**Case 1 — Commit message consistency:** Collect all added `+` diff lines. Extract each unique module label suffix (text after the last `;`, e.g. `NvmeRstPassword_11`). Parse the commit message for those label identifiers. Any changed label that is **not mentioned** anywhere in the commit message → **MAJOR**. Tag `[VEB-LABEL-COMMIT: <N> unexpected entries changed — <list of unmentioned labels>]`. If all changed labels are covered → PASS.\n\n> **Multi-module sync commits:** A commit that bumps multiple packages (e.g., Intel RC sync) must list every changed label in the commit message. Unlisted labels still fire MAJOR.\n\n**Case 2 — SDL version token match:** For each unique changed module label:\n1. Determine the package SDL — e.g., `NvmeRstPassword_11` → `AmiChipsetModulePkg/SB/NvmeRstPassword/NvmeRstPassword.sdl`; `AmiTrustedFvPkg_22` → `AmiTrustedFvPkg/AmiTrustedFvPkg.sdl`. Use the `.cif` path prefix to locate the owning SDL.\n2. `grep_search` the package SDL for any TOKEN block with `_VERSION` or `_REVISION` in its Name and a `Value` field.\n3. **Compare:** Extract the numeric label suffix from the `.veb` entry (e.g., `11` from `NvmeRstPassword_11`). Compare with the token `Value`.\n   - **Match → PASS.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: CONSISTENT — <TOKEN_NAME> = <value>]`.\n   - **Mismatch → MAJOR.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: MISMATCH — .veb label <N> but <TOKEN_NAME> = <M>]`.\n   - **False-positive guard:** If the token name ends in `_REVISION` (not `_VERSION`) **and** the token's Help text contains a cross-reference note mapping revision to label (e.g., `\"Rev59 = SVN label 55\"` or `\"Rev<X> = label<Y>\"`), then a numeric difference between the label and the token value is **intentional and documented**. In this case downgrade to **INFORMATIONAL** and tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: REVISION-OFFSET-NOTED — Help text documents deliberate offset; label <N>, token <TOKEN_NAME> = <M>]`. Do NOT fire MAJOR.\n   - **No version token found → INFORMATIONAL.** Tag `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: NO-TOKEN — no _VERSION or _REVISION SDL token found in <sdl-path>]`. This is expected for Intel RC packages (e.g., `RaptorLakePlatSamplePkg`, `ClientOneSiliconPkg`) which use composite version strings and have no integer SDL token.\n   - **Complex label strings** (e.g., `RaptorLakePlatSamplePkg_0C.00.43.42(7113.00)_066`) — no integer SDL token is expected; skip Case 2 and emit `[VEB-VERSION-TOKEN: NO-TOKEN — Intel RC composite label, no SDL token expected]`.\n\n#### `.dsc`/`.mak`/`.cif`/`.nsh` files\n\n- Copyright year (see §12) · general correctness only\n- For `.dsc` `[PcdsFixedAtBuild]` hunks: if `PcdCpuSmmRestrictedMemoryAccess` is present, confirm it is not `FALSE` in a release build (`DEBUG_MODE = 0`) — raise MAJOR\n"
