     103| ===== FILE: .github\skills\ami-firmware-coding-standards\Firmware_Coding_Standards.md  (924 lines) =====
     104| 00001| # AMI Aptio 5.x Firmware Coding Standards (INFORMATIONAL)
     105| 00002| 
     106| 00003| **Source:** AMI Aptio 5.x Firmware Coding Standards  
     107| 00004| **Compliance Level:** INFORMATIONAL - Style recommendations only  
     108| 00005| **Scope:** Firmware-specific style guidance extending Module Developer's Guide
     109| 00006| 
     110| 00007| ---
     111| 00008| 
     112| 00009| ## Validation Scope: AMI Code Only (INFORMATIONAL)
     113| 00010| 
     114| 00011| These standards are **INFORMATIONAL** style recommendations for AMI-owned code. Violations do NOT impact the final review verdict.
     115| 00012| 
     116| 00013| ### Relationship to Module Developer's Guide
     117| 00014| 
     118| 00015| | Standard | Compliance Level | Impact |
     119| 00016| |----------|------------------|--------|
     120| 00017| | **Module Developer's Guide** | MANDATORY | Violations impact verdict (MAJOR/MINOR) |
     121| 00018| | **Firmware Coding Standards** (this document) | INFORMATIONAL | Violations tracked for post-merge improvement |
     122| 00019| 
     123| 00020| **All Firmware Coding Standards findings use INFO severity.**
     124| 00021| 
     125| 00022| ---
     126| 00023| 
     127| 00024| ## 1. Comment Style and Documentation
     128| 00025| 
     129| 00026| ### Function Header Comments
     130| 00027| 
     131| 00028| **Guideline:** All functions should have complete Doxygen-style header comments.
     132| 00029| 
     133| 00030| ```c
     134| 00031| /**
     135| 00032|   Initialize the NVRAM driver.
     136| 00033| 
     137| 00034|   This function performs the following:
     138| 00035|   - Allocates NVRAM buffers
     139| 00036|   - Registers variable services protocol
     140| 00037|   - Installs NVRAM access protocol
     141| 00038| 
     142| 00039|   @param[in]  ImageHandle   The firmware allocated handle for the EFI image
     143| 00040|   @param[in]  SystemTable   A pointer to the EFI System Table
     144| 00041| 
     145| 00042|   @retval EFI_SUCCESS       NVRAM initialized successfully
     146| 00043|   @retval EFI_OUT_OF_RESOURCES  Failed to allocate buffers
     147| 00044|   @retval EFI_DEVICE_ERROR  NVRAM hardware error
     148| 00045| 
     149| 00046| **/
     150| 00047| EFI_STATUS
     151| 00048| EFIAPI
     152| 00049| NvramDxeInit (
     153| 00050|   IN EFI_HANDLE        ImageHandle,
     154| 00051|   IN EFI_SYSTEM_TABLE  *SystemTable
     155| 00052|   )
     156| 00053| ```
     157| 00054| 
     158| 00055| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     159| 00056| - Missing `@param` tags
     160| 00057| - Missing `@retval` descriptions
     161| 00058| - Missing function purpose description
     162| 00059| - Missing detailed behavior notes
     163| 00060| 
     164| 00061| ### Inline Comments
     165| 00062| 
     166| 00063| **Guideline:** Complex logic should have explanatory comments.
     167| 00064| 
     168| 00065| ✅ **Good:**
     169| 00066| ```c
     170| 00067| // Check if variable is authenticated before allowing delete
     171| 00068| if (!(Attributes & EFI_VARIABLE_AUTHENTICATED_WRITE_ACCESS)) {
     172| 00069|   return EFI_SECURITY_VIOLATION;
     173| 00070| }
     174| 00071| ```
     175| 00072| 
     176| 00073| ⚠️ **Needs Improvement:**
     177| 00074| ```c
     178| 00075| // Check flags
     179| 00076| if (!(Attr & 0x20)) {  // INFO: Magic number, unclear purpose
     180| 00077|   return EFI_SECURITY_VIOLATION;
     181| 00078| }
     182| 00079| ```
     183| 00080| 
     184| 00081| ### TODO/FIXME/HACK Markers
     185| 00082| 
     186| 00083| **Guideline:** Use standardized markers for known issues.
     187| 00084| 
     188| 00085| ```c
     189| 00086| // TODO: Optimize buffer allocation for S3 path
     190| 00087| // FIXME: Race condition when multiple threads access the variable
     191| 00088| // HACK: Temporary workaround for silicon errata, remove in next release
     192| 00089| ```
     193| 00090| 
     194| 00091| ---
     195| 00092| 
     196| 00093| ## 2. Source File Structure
     197| 00094| 
     198| 00095| ### C File Organization
     199| 00096| 
     200| 00097| **Guideline:** C source files must follow this strict order:
     201| 00098| 
     202| 00099| 1. **File Header** (copyright + `@file` block)
     203| 00100| 2. **Include Statements** (grouped and ordered)
     204| 00101| 3. **Constants, Macros, and Type Definitions**
     205| 00102| 4. **Variable and External Declarations**
     206| 00103| 5. **Function Definitions**
     207| 00104| 
     208| 00105| **Rules:**
     209| 00106| - Function prototypes/declarations must appear before function definitions
     210| 00107| - Group related declarations together
     211| 00108| - No mixed ordering (e.g., function definition → variable → function definition)
     212| 00109| - Function definitions should appear in logical order (initialization → helpers → main logic)
     213| 00110| 
     214| 00111| ✅ **Good Structure:**
     215| 00112| ```c
     216| 00113| //***********************************************************************
     217| 00114| // File Header
     218| 00115| //***********************************************************************
     219| 00116| 
     220| 00117| // Include(s)
     221| 00118| #include <Uefi.h>
     222| 00119| #include <Library/BaseLib.h>
     223| 00120| 
     224| 00121| // Constant Definition(s)
     225| 00122| #define MAX_SIZE  256
     226| 00123| 
     227| 00124| // Type Definition(s)
     228| 00125| typedef struct {
     229| 00126|   UINT32  Value;
     230| 00127| } MY_STRUCT;
     231| 00128| 
     232| 00129| // Function Prototype(s)
     233| 00130| EFI_STATUS HelperFunction(VOID);
     234| 00131| EFI_STATUS MainFunction(VOID);
     235| 00132| 
     236| 00133| // Variable Declaration(s)
     237| 00134| STATIC UINT32  mCounter = 0;
     238| 00135| 
     239| 00136| // Function Definition(s)
     240| 00137| EFI_STATUS
     241| 00138| HelperFunction (
     242| 00139|   VOID
     243| 00140|   )
     244| 00141| {
     245| 00142|   // Implementation
     246| 00143| }
     247| 00144| 
     248| 00145| EFI_STATUS
     249| 00146| MainFunction (
     250| 00147|   VOID
     251| 00148|   )
     252| 00149| {
     253| 00150|   // Implementation
     254| 00151| }
     255| 00152| ```
     256| 00153| 
     257| 00154| ⚠️ **Poor Structure (INFO):**
     258| 00155| ```c
     259| 00156| // Function definition before declaration
     260| 00157| EFI_STATUS SomeFunction(VOID) { ... }  // INFO: Declare before define
     261| 00158| 
     262| 00159| // Variable after function
     263| 00160| STATIC UINT32 mVar;  // INFO: Variables should come before functions
     264| 00161| 
     265| 00162| // Another function
     266| 00163| EFI_STATUS AnotherFunction(VOID) { ... }
     267| 00164| ```
     268| 00165| 
     269| 00166| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     270| 00167| - Mixed ordering of declarations and definitions
     271| 00168| - Function definitions before declarations
     272| 00169| - Variables scattered throughout file
     273| 00170| - Related functions not grouped
     274| 00171| 
     275| 00172| ---
     276| 00173| 
     277| 00174| ## 3. Header File Rules
     278| 00175| 
     279| 00176| ### No Code in Headers
     280| 00177| 
     281| 00178| **Guideline:** Header files (`.h`) must contain ONLY declarations, never code implementations.
     282| 00179| 
     283| 00180| ❌ **Prohibited in Headers:**
     284| 00181| ```c
     285| 00182| // MyHeader.h
     286| 00183| void MyFunction() {  // INFO: Function definition in header
     287| 00184|   DoSomething();
     288| 00185| }
     289| 00186| 
     290| 00187| STATIC UINT32 mVariable = 0;  // INFO: Variable definition in header
     291| 00188| ```
     292| 00189| 
     293| 00190| ✅ **Correct:**
     294| 00191| ```c
     295| 00192| // MyHeader.h
     296| 00193| void MyFunction(VOID);  // Declaration only
     297| 00194| 
     298| 00195| extern UINT32 mVariable;  // External declaration
     299| 00196| ```
     300| 00197| 
     301| 00198| ### Include Guards
     302| 00199| 
     303| 00200| **Guideline:** All header files must use include guards.
     304| 00201| 
     305| 00202| ✅ **Required Pattern:**
     306| 00203| ```c
     307| 00204| #ifndef _MY_HEADER_H_
     308| 00205| #define _MY_HEADER_H_
     309| 00206| 
     310| 00207| // Header content
     311| 00208| 
     312| 00209| #endif  // _MY_HEADER_H_
     313| 00210| ```
     314| 00211| 
     315| 00212| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     316| 00213| - Missing include guards
     317| 00214| - Incorrect guard naming (should match filename)
     318| 00215| - Missing closing `#endif` comment
     319| 00216| 
     320| 00217| ### Self-Contained Headers
     321| 00218| 
     322| 00219| **Guideline:** Headers should be self-contained and include all dependencies.
     323| 00220| 
     324| 00221| ✅ **Good:**
     325| 00222| ```c
     326| 00223| // MyProtocol.h
     327| 00224| #include <Uefi.h>  // Needed for EFI_STATUS
     328| 00225| 
     329| 00226| EFI_STATUS InstallMyProtocol(VOID);
     330| 00227| ```
     331| 00228| 
     332| 00229| ⚠️ **Needs Improvement:**
     333| 00230| ```c
     334| 00231| // MyProtocol.h
     335| 00232| EFI_STATUS InstallMyProtocol(VOID);  // INFO: Missing <Uefi.h> for EFI_STATUS
     336| 00233| ```
     337| 00234| 
     338| 00235| ### Minimize Header Includes
     339| 00236| 
     340| 00237| **Guideline:** Include only what is directly needed in the header.
     341| 00238| 
     342| 00239| - Avoid including headers that are only needed by the `.c` implementation
     343| 00240| - Use forward declarations when possible
     344| 00241| - Separate public vs private definitions (use separate headers if needed)
     345| 00242| 
     346| 00243| ✅ **Good:**
     347| 00244| ```c
     348| 00245| // MyPublic.h - Public interface
     349| 00246| typedef struct _MY_PROTOCOL MY_PROTOCOL;  // Forward declaration
     350| 00247| 
     351| 00248| EFI_STATUS InstallProtocol(MY_PROTOCOL *Protocol);
     352| 00249| ```
     353| 00250| 
     354| 00251| ---
     355| 00252| 
     356| 00253| ## 4. Source Line Formatting
     357| 00254| 
     358| 00255| ### One Statement Per Line
     359| 00256| 
     360| 00257| **Guideline:** Each statement should be on its own line.
     361| 00258| 
     362| 00259| ❌ **Avoid:**
     363| 00260| ```c
     364| 00261| Status = Init(); if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) return Status;  // INFO: Split into multiple lines
     365| 00262| ```
     366| 00263| 
     367| 00264| ✅ **Good:**
     368| 00265| ```c
     369| 00266| Status = Init();
     370| 00267| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     371| 00268|   return Status;
     372| 00269| }
     373| 00270| ```
     374| 00271| 
     375| 00272| ### Operator Spacing
     376| 00273| 
     377| 00274| **Guideline:** Consistent spacing around operators improves readability.
     378| 00275| 
     379| 00276| ✅ **Good Spacing:**
     380| 00277| ```c
     381| 00278| Result = Value1 + Value2;       // Space around binary operators
     382| 00279| Pointer->Member;                // No space around ->
     383| 00280| Structure.Field;                // No space around .
     384| 00281| Array[Index];                   // No space before [
     385| 00282| Function(Arg1, Arg2);           // Space after comma
     386| 00283| for (i = 0; i < Max; i++);      // Space after semicolon
     387| 00284| ```
     388| 00285| 
     389| 00286| ⚠️ **Inconsistent (INFO):**
     390| 00287| ```c
     391| 00288| Result=Value1+Value2;           // INFO: Add spaces
     392| 00289| Pointer -> Member;              // INFO: Remove spaces
     393| 00290| Function(Arg1,Arg2);            // INFO: Add space after comma
     394| 00291| ```
     395| 00292| 
     396| 00293| ### Variable Declarations
     397| 00294| 
     398| 00295| **Guideline:** One variable per line (except related simple variables).
     399| 00296| 
     400| 00297| ✅ **Preferred:**
     401| 00298| ```c
     402| 00299| UINT32  BufferSize;
     403| 00300| UINT32  MaxSize;
     404| 00301| UINT8   *Buffer;
     405| 00302| ```
     406| 00303| 
     407| 00304| ⚠️ **Avoid:**
     408| 00305| ```c
     409| 00306| UINT32 BufferSize, MaxSize, *Pointer;  // INFO: Split into separate lines
     410| 00307| ```
     411| 00308| 
     412| 00309| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     413| 00310| - Multiple variables declared on one line
     414| 00311| - Inconsistent spacing in declarations
     415| 00312| - Mixed types on same line
     416| 00313| 
     417| 00314| ---
     418| 00315| 
     419| 00316| ## 5. Naming Quality
     420| 00317| 
     421| 00318| ### Meaningful Names
     422| 00319| 
     423| 00320| **Guideline:** Use descriptive, unambiguous names that convey purpose.
     424| 00321| 
     425| 00322| ❌ **Avoid Ambiguous Names:**
     426| 00323| ```c
     427| 00324| UINT32  Size1, Size2;           // INFO: What do these sizes represent?
     428| 00325| UINT32  Var1, Var2, Var3;       // INFO: Non-descriptive
     429| 00326| UINT32  Temp, Tmp, T;           // INFO: Overly abbreviated
     430| 00327| ```
     431| 00328| 
     432| 00329| ✅ **Better:**
     433| 00330| ```c
     434| 00331| UINT32  InputBufferSize;
     435| 00332| UINT32  OutputBufferSize;
     436| 00333| UINT32  MaxTransferSize;
     437| 00334| ```
     438| 00335| 
     439| 00336| ### Avoid Similar Names
     440| 00337| 
     441| 00338| **Guideline:** Prevent confusion from similar-looking identifiers.
     442| 00339| 
     443| 00340| ⚠️ **Confusing (INFO):**
     444| 00341| ```c
     445| 00342| UINT32  BufferSize;             // Lower camel case
     446| 00343| UINT32  buffersize;             // All lowercase - INFO: Too similar
     447| 00344| UINT32  BUFFERSIZE;             // All caps - INFO: Case-only difference
     448| 00345| UINT32  Buffer_Size;            // Underscore variant - INFO: Inconsistent
     449| 00346| ```
     450| 00347| 
     451| 00348| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     452| 00349| - Case-only differences between identifiers
     453| 00350| - Similar names with minor variations
     454| 00351| - Single-letter differences (e.g., `DataPtr` vs `DataPrt`)
     455| 00352| 
     456| 00353| ### Appropriate Abbreviations
     457| 00354| 
     458| 00355| **Guideline:** Use well-known abbreviations; avoid cryptic short forms.
     459| 00356| 
     460| 00357| ✅ **Acceptable Abbreviations:**
     461| 00358| - `Max`, `Min`, `Num`, `Ptr`, `Addr`, `Len`, `Idx`
     462| 00359| - `Init`, `Cfg`, `Tmp`, `Mgr`, `Ctrl`
     463| 00360| 
     464| 00361| ⚠️ **Overly Abbreviated (INFO):**
     465| 00362| ```c
     466| 00363| UINT32  BufSz;                  // INFO: Use BufferSize
     467| 00364| UINT32  NmElmnts;               // INFO: Use NumElements
     468| 00365| EFI_STATUS  Sts;                // INFO: Use Status
     469| 00366| ```
     470| 00367| 
     471| 00368| **Observations (INFO severity):**
     472| 00369| - Unclear abbreviations
     473| 00370| - Inconsistent abbreviation style within same file
     474| 00371| - Names too short to be meaningful
     475| 00372| 
     476| 00373| ---
     477| 00374| 
     478| 00375| ## 6. Third-Party Code Modification (Porting Markers)
     479| 00376| 
     480| 00377| ### AMI Porting Markers - REQUIRED
     481| 00378| 
     482| 00379| **Guideline:** ALL modifications to third-party or EDK2 code MUST be wrapped with AMI porting markers.
     483| 00380| 
     484| 00381| **Required Pattern:**
     485| 00382| ```c
     486| 00383| //*** AMI PORTING BEGIN ***
     487| 00384| // Modified code here
     488| 00385| //*** AMI PORTING END ***
     489| 00386| ```
     490| 00387| 
     491| 00388| **Applies to:**
     492| 00389| - EDK2 packages (`MdePkg`, `MdeModulePkg`, `SecurityPkg`, `CryptoPkg`, `UefiCpuPkg`)
     493| 00390| - Intel packages (`Intel/`)
     494| 00391| - Any third-party code not owned by AMI
     495| 00392| 
     496| 00393| ✅ **Correct Usage:**
     497| 00394| ```c
     498| 00395| // Original Intel/EDK2 code
     499| 00396| void OriginalFunction()
     500| 00397| {
     501| 00398|   // Original implementation
     502| 00399|   
     503| 00400|   //*** AMI PORTING BEGIN ***
     504| 00401|   // AMI-specific validation added
     505| 00402|   if (!ValidateAmiRequirement()) {
     506| 00403|     return EFI_SECURITY_VIOLATION;
     507| 00404|   }
     508| 00405|   //*** AMI PORTING END ***
     509| 00406|   
     510| 00407|   // Rest of original code
     511| 00408| }
     512| 00409| ```
     513| 00410| 
     514| 00411| ❌ **Missing Markers (INFO):**
     515| 00412| ```c
     516| 00413| // Modified third-party code without markers
     517| 00414| void ThirdPartyFunction()
     518| 00415| {
     519| 00416|   // Original code
     520| 00417|   CustomAmiFunction();  // INFO: AMI modification not marked
     521| 00418|   // Original code
     522| 00419| }
     523| 00420| ```
     524| 00421| 
     525| 00422| ### Marker Placement Rules
     526| 00423| 
     527| 00424| 1. **Wrap only AMI changes** - Do not include original code inside markers
     528| 00425| 2. **One marker pair per change** - Separate distinct modifications
     529| 00426| 3. **Add brief description** - Explain why modification was needed
     530| 00427| 4. **Keep markers minimal** - Only changed lines, not entire functions
     531| 00428| 
     532| 00429| ✅ **Good:**
     533| 00430| ```c
     534| 00431| Status = AllocateBuffer();
     535| 00432| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     536| 00433|   //*** AMI PORTING BEGIN ***
     537| 00434|   // Added logging for debug tracking
     538| 00435|   DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "[AMI] Buffer allocation failed: %r\n", Status));
     539| 00436|   //*** AMI PORTING END ***
     540| 00437|   return Status;
     541| 00438| }
     542| 00439| ```
     543| 00440| 
     544| 00441| ### Alternative Marker Names
     545| 00442| 
     546| 00443| These are also acceptable (project-specific):
     547| 00444| - `//*** AMI PORTING BEGIN ***` / `//*** AMI PORTING END ***` (preferred)
     548| 00445| - `// AMI OVERRIDE START` / `// AMI OVERRIDE END`
     549| 00446| - `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:` / `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_END:`
     550| 00447| 
     551| 00448| **Observation (INFO severity):**
     552| 00449| - Modifications to third-party code without porting markers
     553| 00450| - Incorrect marker syntax
     554| 00451| - Missing explanation in marker comments
     555| 00452| - Markers wrapping too much unmodified code
     556| 00453| 
     557| 00454| ---
     558| 00455| 
     559| 00456| ## 7. Code Readability
     560| 00457| 
     561| 00458| ### Line Length
     562| 00459| 
     563| 00460| **Guideline:** Prefer lines under 120 characters.
     564| 00461| 
     565| 00462| **Observation:** Lines exceeding 120 characters reduce readability (INFO severity).
     566| 00463| 
     567| 00464| ✅ **Good:**
     568| 00465| ```c
     569| 00466| Status = gBS->InstallMultipleProtocolInterfaces(
     570| 00467|                 &Handle,
     571| 00468|                 &gEfiNvramAccessProtocolGuid,
     572| 00469|                 &mNvramAccessProtocol,
     573| 00470|                 NULL
     574| 00471|                 );
     575| 00472| ```
     576| 00473| 
     577| 00474| ⚠️ **Consider Refactoring:**
     578| 00475| ```c
     579| 00476| Status = gBS->InstallMultipleProtocolInterfaces(&Handle, &gEfiNvramAccessProtocolGuid, &mNvramAccessProtocol, &gEfiNvramControlProtocolGuid, &mNvramControlProtocol, NULL);  // INFO: Line too long
     580| 00477| ```
     581| 00478| 
     582| 00479| ### Function Length
     583| 00480| 
     584| 00481| **Guideline:** Functions should be under 200 lines.
     585| 00482| 
     586| 00483| **Observation:** Functions exceeding 200 lines suggest refactoring opportunities (INFO severity).
     587| 00484| 
     588| 00485| **Suggestion:** Break into smaller, focused functions:
     589| 00486| - Extract complex logic into helper functions
     590| 00487| - Separate initialization from processing
     591| 00488| - Create subfunctions for error handling paths
     592| 00489| 
     593| 00490| ### Nesting Depth
     594| 00491| 
     595| 00492| **Guideline:** Prefer nesting depth under 5 levels.
     596| 00493| 
     597| 00494| ⚠️ **Deep Nesting (INFO):**
     598| 00495| ```c
     599| 00496| if (Condition1) {
     600| 00497|   if (Condition2) {
     601| 00498|     if (Condition3) {
     602| 00499|       if (Condition4) {
     603| 00500|         if (Condition5) {
     604| 00501|           // INFO: Consider refactoring (5+ levels deep)
     605| 00502|         }
     606| 00503|       }
     607| 00504|     }
     608| 00505|   }
     609| 00506| }
     610| 00507| ```
     611| 00508| 
     612| 00509| ✅ **Better - Early Returns:**
     613| 00510| ```c
     614| 00511| if (!Condition1) return EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER;
     615| 00512| if (!Condition2) return EFI_NOT_READY;
     616| 00513| if (!Condition3) return EFI_DEVICE_ERROR;
     617| 00514| if (!Condition4) return EFI_ACCESS_DENIED;
     618| 00515| // Actual logic at minimal nesting
     619| 00516| ```
     620| 00517| 
     621| 00518| ### Variable Scope Minimization
     622| 00519| 
     623| 00520| **Guideline:** Declare variables in the smallest scope possible.
     624| 00521| 
     625| 00522| ✅ **Good:**
     626| 00523| ```c
     627| 00524| EFI_STATUS MyFunction(VOID)
     628| 00525| {
     629| 00526|   EFI_STATUS  Status;
     630| 00527|   
     631| 00528|   // ... some code ...
     632| 00529|   
     633| 00530|   {
     634| 00531|     UINT32  TempValue;  // Scoped to this block only
     635| 00532|     TempValue = CalculateSomething();
     636| 00533|     Status = ProcessValue(TempValue);
     637| 00534|   }
     638| 00535|   
     639| 00536|   return Status;
     640| 00537| }
     641| 00538| ```
     642| 00539| 
     643| 00540| ---
     644| 00541| 
     645| 00542| ## 8. Error Handling Patterns
     646| 00543| 
     647| 00544| ### Consistent Error Handling
     648| 00545| 
     649| 00546| **Guideline:** Use consistent error handling patterns throughout a module.
     650| 00547| 
     651| 00548| ✅ **Consistent Pattern:**
     652| 00549| ```c
     653| 00550| Status = Step1();
     654| 00551| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     655| 00552|   DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "Step1 failed: %r\n", Status));
     656| 00553|   goto Exit;
     657| 00554| }
     658| 00555| 
     659| 00556| Status = Step2();
     660| 00557| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     661| 00558|   DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "Step2 failed: %r\n", Status));
     662| 00559|   goto Exit;
     663| 00560| }
     664| 00561| 
     665| 00562| Exit:
     666| 00563|   // Cleanup
     667| 00564|   return Status;
     668| 00565| ```
     669| 00566| 
     670| 00567| ### Resource Cleanup
     671| 00568| 
     672| 00569| **Guideline:** Always clean up resources in error paths.
     673| 00570| 
     674| 00571| ✅ **Good - Cleanup on Error:**
     675| 00572| ```c
     676| 00573| Buffer = AllocatePool(Size);
     677| 00574| if (Buffer == NULL) {
     678| 00575|   return EFI_OUT_OF_RESOURCES;
     679| 00576| }
     680| 00577| 
     681| 00578| Status = ProcessBuffer(Buffer);
     682| 00579| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     683| 00580|   FreePool(Buffer);  // Cleanup before return
     684| 00581|   return Status;
     685| 00582| }
     686| 00583| 
     687| 00584| FreePool(Buffer);
     688| 00585| return EFI_SUCCESS;
     689| 00586| ```
     690| 00587| 
     691| 00588| ### Error Message Clarity
     692| 00589| 
     693| 00590| **Guideline:** Debug messages should clearly identify the error source.
     694| 00591| 
     695| 00592| ✅ **Good:**
     696| 00593| ```c
     697| 00594| DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "[NVRAM] Failed to allocate buffer (Size=%d): %r\n", BufferSize, Status));
     698| 00595| ```
     699| 00596| 
     700| 00597| ⚠️ **Needs Improvement:**
     701| 00598| ```c
     702| 00599| DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "Error: %r\n", Status));  // INFO: Add context (module, operation)
     703| 00600| ```
     704| 00601| 
     705| 00602| ---
     706| 00603| 
     707| 00604| ## 9. Performance Considerations
     708| 00605| 
     709| 00606| ### Unnecessary Memory Allocations
     710| 00607| 
     711| 00608| **Guideline:** Avoid allocations in performance-critical paths.
     712| 00609| 
     713| 00610| ⚠️ **Optimization Opportunity (INFO):**
     714| 00611| ```c
     715| 00612| for (Index = 0; Index < Count; Index++) {
     716| 00613|   Buffer = AllocatePool(Size);  // INFO: Consider allocating once before loop
     717| 00614|   ProcessBuffer(Buffer);
     718| 00615|   FreePool(Buffer);
     719| 00616| }
     720| 00617| ```
     721| 00618| 
     722| 00619| ✅ **Better:**
     723| 00620| ```c
     724| 00621| Buffer = AllocatePool(Size);
     725| 00622| for (Index = 0; Index < Count; Index++) {
     726| 00623|   ProcessBuffer(Buffer);
     727| 00624| }
     728| 00625| FreePool(Buffer);
     729| 00626| ```
     730| 00627| 
     731| 00628| ### Repeated Calculations
     732| 00629| 
     733| 00630| **Guideline:** Cache calculated values instead of recalculating.
     734| 00631| 
     735| 00632| ⚠️ **Repeated Calculation (INFO):**
     736| 00633| ```c
     737| 00634| for (Index = 0; Index < Count; Index++) {
     738| 00635|   Process(Data[Index] * sizeof(ELEMENT_TYPE));  // INFO: Calculate once
     739| 00636| }
     740| 00637| ```
     741| 00638| 
     742| 00639| ✅ **Better:**
     743| 00640| ```c
     744| 00641| ElementSize = sizeof(ELEMENT_TYPE);
     745| 00642| for (Index = 0; Index < Count; Index++) {
     746| 00643|   Process(Data[Index] * ElementSize);
     747| 00644| }
     748| 00645| ```
     749| 00646| 
     750| 00647| ### String Operations in Loops
     751| 00648| 
     752| 00649| **Guideline:** Minimize string operations in tight loops.
     753| 00650| 
     754| 00651| ⚠️ **Performance Note (INFO):**
     755| 00652| ```c
     756| 00653| for (Index = 0; Index < Count; Index++) {
     757| 00654|   StrCpy(Buffer, L"Prefix");  // INFO: Move string ops outside loop if possible
     758| 00655|   StrCat(Buffer, Names[Index]);
     759| 00656|   ProcessString(Buffer);
     760| 00657| }
     761| 00658| ```
     762| 00659| 
     763| 00660| ---
     764| 00661| 
     765| 00662| ## 10. Maintainability
     766| 00663| 
     767| 00664| ### Code Duplication
     768| 00665| 
     769| 00666| **Guideline:** Extract common code into reusable functions.
     770| 00667| 
     771| 00668| ⚠️ **Duplication Detected (INFO):**
     772| 00669| ```c
     773| 00670| // In Function1:
     774| 00671| Status = ValidateInput(Input);
     775| 00672| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     776| 00673|   DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "Invalid input: %r\n", Status));
     777| 00674|   return Status;
     778| 00675| }
     779| 00676| 
     780| 00677| // In Function2:
     781| 00678| Status = ValidateInput(Input);  // INFO: Extract to helper function
     782| 00679| if (EFI_ERROR(Status)) {
     783| 00680|   DEBUG((DEBUG_ERROR, "Invalid input: %r\n", Status));
     784| 00681|   return Status;
     785| 00682| }
     786| 00683| ```
     787| 00684| 
     788| 00685| ### Magic Numbers
     789| 00686| 
     790| 00687| **Guideline:** Replace magic numbers with named constants.
     791| 00688| 
     792| 00689| ⚠️ **Magic Number (INFO):**
     793| 00690| ```c
     794| 00691| if (Size > 0x10000) {  // INFO: Use named constant
     795| 00692|   return EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;
     796| 00693| }
     797| 00694| ```
     798| 00695| 
     799| 00696| ✅ **Better:**
     800| 00697| ```c
     801| 00698| #define MAX_BUFFER_SIZE  0x10000  // 64 KB
     802| 00699| 
     803| 00700| if (Size > MAX_BUFFER_SIZE) {
     804| 00701|   return EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;
     805| 00702| }
     806| 00703| ```
     807| 00704| 
     808| 00705| ### Complex Boolean Expressions
     809| 00706| 
     810| 00707| **Guideline:** Simplify complex conditions for clarity.
     811| 00708| 
     812| 00709| ⚠️ **Complex Expression (INFO):**
     813| 00710| ```c
     814| 00711| if ((Flags & FLAG_A) && (Flags & FLAG_B) && !(Flags & FLAG_C) && 
     815| 00712|     (Status == EFI_SUCCESS || Status == EFI_WARN_RESET_REQUIRED)) {
     816| 00713|   // INFO: Consider extracting to named boolean or helper function
     817| 00714| }
     818| 00715| ```
     819| 00716| 
     820| 00717| ✅ **Better:**
     821| 00718| ```c
     822| 00719| BOOLEAN IsValidState(UINT32 Flags, EFI_STATUS Status)
     823| 00720| {
     824| 00721|   if (!(Flags & FLAG_A) || !(Flags & FLAG_B)) return FALSE;
     825| 00722|   if (Flags & FLAG_C) return FALSE;
     826| 00723|   if (Status != EFI_SUCCESS && Status != EFI_WARN_RESET_REQUIRED) return FALSE;
     827| 00724|   return TRUE;
     828| 00725| }
     829| 00726| 
     830| 00727| if (IsValidState(Flags, Status)) {
     831| 00728|   // Clear logic
     832| 00729| }
     833| 00730| ```
     834| 00731| 
     835| 00732| ---
     836| 00733| 
     837| 00734| ## 11. Firmware-Specific Patterns
     838| 00735| 
     839| 00736| ### Boot Path Optimization
     840| 00737| 
     841| 00738| **Guideline:** Optimize boot path for minimal delay.
     842| 00739| 
     843| 00740| **Observations (INFO):**
     844| 00741| - Defer non-critical initialization to later boot phases
     845| 00742| - Minimize PEI phase memory allocations
     846| 00743| - Avoid unnecessary protocol installs in early boot
     847| 00744| - Cache frequently accessed data
     848| 00745| 
     849| 00746| **Example:**
     850| 00747| ```c
     851| 00748| // INFO: Consider deferring feature init to BDS phase
     852| 00749| if (IsBootPhase(DXE_CORE)) {
     853| 00750|   // Defer non-critical features
     854| 00751|   RegisterProtocolNotify(&gEfiBdsArchProtocolGuid, DeferredInit);
     855| 00752| } else {
     856| 00753|   // Critical path only
     857| 00754|   InitializeCriticalHardware();
     858| 00755| }
     859| 00756| ```
     860| 00757| 
     861| 00758| ### Memory Footprint
     862| 00759| 
     863| 00760| **Guideline:** Minimize memory usage, especially in PEI.
     864| 00761| 
     865| 00762| **Observations (INFO):**
     866| 00763| - Large static arrays suggest pool allocation
     867| 00764| - Temporary buffers should be freed promptly
     868| 00765| - Consider pool vs page allocation based on size
     869| 00766| - PEI HOBs should be minimal
     870| 00767| 
     871| 00768| **Example:**
     872| 00769| ```c
     873| 00770| // INFO: Large array increases footprint
     874| 00771| STATIC UINT8 mLargeBuffer[64 * 1024];  // 64KB static allocation
     875| 00772| 
     876| 00773| // Consider:
     877| 00774| UINT8  *Buffer = AllocatePool(RequiredSize);  // Allocate only what's needed
     878| 00775| ```
     879| 00776| 
     880| 00777| ### S3 Resume Path Safety
     881| 00778| 
     882| 00779| **Guideline:** Ensure S3 resume path uses only S3-safe resources.
     883| 00780| 
     884| 00781| **Observations (INFO):**
     885| 00782| - No runtime variable access in S3 path (use boot script)
     886| 00783| - No protocol dependencies in S3 resume
     887| 00784| - Hardware state must be restored from saved boot script
     888| 00785| - SMM handlers must be S3-aware
     889| 00786| 
     890| 00787| **Example:**
     891| 00788| ```c
     892| 00789| // INFO: Variable access not S3-safe
     893| 00790| if (IsS3Resume()) {
     894| 00791|   // Use boot script data, not fresh variable reads
     895| 00792|   RestoreFromBootScript();
     896| 00793| } else {
     897| 00794|   GetVariable(L"Config", ...);
     898| 00795| }
     899| 00796| ```
     900| 00797| 
     901| 00798| ---
     902| 00799| 
     903| 00800| ## 12. Additional Style Recommendations
     904| 00801| 
     905| 00802| ### Whitespace
     906| 00803| 
     907| 00804| **Guideline:** Consistent whitespace improves readability.
     908| 00805| 
     909| 00806| - Blank line between function definitions
     910| 00807| - Blank line between logical code blocks
     911| 00808| - Space after keywords: `if (`, `while (`, `for (`
     912| 00809| - No trailing whitespace
     913| 00810| 
     914| 00811| ### Bracket Style
     915| 00812| 
     916| 00813| **Guideline:** Follow consistent bracket placement.
     917| 00814| 
     918| 00815| ✅ **Preferred (UEFI Style):**
     919| 00816| ```c
     920| 00817| if (Condition)
     921| 00818| {
     922| 00819|   // Code
     923| 00820| }
     924| 00821| ```
     925| 00822| 
     926| 00823| **Acceptable:**
     927| 00824| ```c
     928| 00825| if (Condition) {
     929| 00826|   // Code
     930| 00827| }
     931| 00828| ```
     932| 00829| 
     933| 00830| **Choose one and be consistent within a file.**
     934| 00831| 
     935| 00832| ### Typedef vs Struct
     936| 00833| 
     937| 00834| **Guideline:** Use typedefs for complex structures.
     938| 00835| 
     939| 00836| ✅ **Good:**
     940| 00837| ```c
     941| 00838| typedef struct {
     942| 00839|   UINT32  Field1;
     943| 00840|   UINT16  Field2;
     944| 00841| } MY_STRUCTURE;
     945| 00842| 
     946| 00843| MY_STRUCTURE  MyVar;  // Clean usage
     947| 00844| ```
     948| 00845| 
     949| 00846| ---
     950| 00847| 
     951| 00848| ## Validation Checklist (All INFO Severity)
     952| 00849| 
     953| 00850| When reviewing for Firmware Coding Standards:
     954| 00851| 
     955| 00852| ☐ **Comments**
     956| 00853|   - [ ] Function headers complete with @param/@retval
     957| 00854|   - [ ] Complex logic has explanatory comments
     958| 00855|   - [ ] TODO/FIXME properly marked
     959| 00856| 
     960| 00857| ☐ **File Structure**
     961| 00858|   - [ ] C files follow correct order (header → includes → constants → variables → functions)
     962| 00859|   - [ ] Function declarations before definitions
     963| 00860|   - [ ] No mixed ordering of sections
     964| 00861|   - [ ] Related declarations grouped together
     965| 00862| 
     966| 00863| ☐ **Header Files**
     967| 00864|   - [ ] No code implementations in headers (declarations only)
     968| 00865|   - [ ] Include guards present and correctly named
     969| 00866|   - [ ] Headers are self-contained
     970| 00867|   - [ ] Unnecessary includes minimized
     971| 00868| 
     972| 00869| ☐ **Line Formatting**
     973| 00870|   - [ ] One statement per line
     974| 00871|   - [ ] Consistent operator spacing
     975| 00872|   - [ ] One variable per line (exceptions for related simple vars)
     976| 00873|   - [ ] No trailing whitespace
     977| 00874| 
     978| 00875| ☐ **Naming Quality**
     979| 00876|   - [ ] Names are meaningful and descriptive
     980| 00877|   - [ ] No ambiguous names (Size1, Var2, etc.)
     981| 00878|   - [ ] No case-only name differences
     982| 00879|   - [ ] Abbreviations are clear and consistent
     983| 00880| 
     984| 00881| ☐ **Porting Markers**
     985| 00882|   - [ ] AMI modifications to third-party code wrapped with `//*** AMI PORTING BEGIN/END ***`
     986| 00883|   - [ ] Markers include brief explanation
     987| 00884|   - [ ] Only changed code inside markers
     988| 00885|   - [ ] Correct syntax used
     989| 00886| 
     990| 00887| ☐ **Readability**
     991| 00888|   - [ ] Lines under 120 characters (where reasonable)
     992| 00889|   - [ ] Functions under 200 lines
     993| 00890|   - [ ] Nesting depth under 5 levels
     994| 00891|   - [ ] Variables scoped minimally
     995| 00892| 
     996| 00893| ☐ **Error Handling**
     997| 00894|   - [ ] Consistent error handling pattern
     998| 00895|   - [ ] All error paths clean up resources
     999| 00896|   - [ ] Error messages are clear and specific
    1000| 00897| 
    1001| 00898| ☐ **Performance**
    1002| 00899|   - [ ] No unnecessary allocations in loops
    1003| 00900|   - [ ] Calculations cached when repeated
    1004| 00901|   - [ ] String operations minimized in tight loops
    1005| 00902| 
    1006| 00903| ☐ **Maintainability**
    1007| 00904|   - [ ] No significant code duplication
    1008| 00905|   - [ ] Magic numbers replaced with constants
    1009| 00906|   - [ ] Complex expressions simplified
    1010| 00907| 
    1011| 00908| ☐ **Firmware-Specific**
    1012| 00909|   - [ ] Boot path optimized (deferred initialization)
    1013| 00910|   - [ ] Memory footprint considered
    1014| 00911|   - [ ] S3 resume path uses safe resources only

    1040| 00010| ## Purpose
    1041| 00011| Validate reviewed code against **informational** AMI Aptio 5.x Firmware Coding Standards that provide additional style guidance beyond Module Developer's Guide requirements.
    1042| 00012| 
    1043| 00013| **Compliance Level:** INFORMATIONAL - Violations do NOT impact the final review verdict. Findings are tracked for post-merge cleanup.
    1044| 00014| 
    1045| 00015| ## When to Use
    1046| 00016| - **After Module Developer's Guide validation** (Step 3.8 complete)
    1047| 00017| - To check firmware-specific style and best practices
    1048| 00018| - Only on files that were already reviewed and passed Module Developer Guide validation
    1049| 00019| 
    1050| 00020| ## Scope
    1051| 00021| This skill checks **firmware-specific style recommendations** only. UEFI/PI/EDK2 spec compliance and Module Developer Guide mandatory standards are already covered.
    1052| 00022| 
    1053| 00023| ## Standards Reference
    1054| 00024| See [Firmware Coding Standards](./Firmware_Coding_Standards.md) for complete firmware-specific style recommendations.
    1055| 00025| 
    1056| 00026| ## Validation Procedure
    1057| 00027| 
    1058| 00028| ### Step 1: Identify Files in Scope
    1059| 00029| Review only files that were checked in Module Developer Guide validation (Step 3.8). Do not review files that were skipped or excluded.
    1060| 00030| 
    1061| 00031| ### Step 2: Classify File Ownership (AMI vs Third-Party)
    1062| 00032| 
    1063| 00033| Use the same classification logic as Module Developer Guide:
    1064| 00034| 
    1065| 00035| **Classification Rules:**
    1066| 00036| 
    1067| 00037| | Condition | Classification | Validation Scope |
    1068| 00038| |-----------|----------------|------------------|
    1069| 00039| | File contains AMI copyright banner (`Copyright (c) 1985-20XX, AMI`) | ✅ **AMI-owned** | Entire file |
    1070| 00040| | File contains third-party copyright AND contains AMI override markers | ⚙️ **Third-party with AMI overrides** | AMI override sections only |
    1071| 00041| | File contains NO copyright header | ✅ **AMI-owned** (default assumption) | Entire file |
    1072| 00042| | File contains only third-party copyright, NO AMI override markers | ❌ **Third-party only** | Skip validation |
    1073| 00043| 
    1074| 00044| **AMI Override Marker Patterns (case-insensitive):**
    1075| 00045| 
    1076| 00046| | Start Marker | End Marker |
    1077| 00047| |--------------|------------|
    1078| 00048| | `// AMI OVERRIDE START` | `// AMI OVERRIDE END` |
    1079| 00049| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_END:` |
    1080| 00050| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_END:` |
    1081| 00051| 
    1082| 00052| ### Step 3: Extract AMI Code Sections
    1083| 00053| 
    1084| 00054| Same extraction logic as Module Developer Guide validation (entire file vs override sections only).
    1085| 00055| 
    1086| 00056| ### Step 4: Check Firmware Coding Standards
    1087| 00057| 
    1088| 00058| For each AMI code section, verify firmware-specific style recommendations:
    1089| 00059| 
    1090| 00060| 1. **Comment Style** (INFORMATIONAL)
    1091| 00061|    - Function header comments completeness
    1092| 00062|    - Code comment clarity and usefulness
    1093| 00063|    - TODO/FIXME/HACK marker usage
    1094| 00064| 
    1095| 00065| 2. **Code Readability** (INFORMATIONAL)
    1096| 00066|    - Line length recommendations (prefer < 120 characters)
    1097| 00067|    - Function length guidelines (prefer < 200 lines)
    1098| 00068|    - Nesting depth (prefer < 5 levels)
    1099| 00069|    - Variable scope minimization
    1100| 00070| 
    1101| 00071| 3. **Error Handling Patterns** (INFORMATIONAL)
    1102| 00072|    - Consistent error handling style
    1103| 00073|    - Resource cleanup in error paths
    1104| 00074|    - Error message clarity
    1105| 00075| 
    1106| 00076| 4. **Performance Considerations** (INFORMATIONAL)
    1107| 00077|    - Unnecessary memory allocations
    1108| 00078|    - Repeated calculations that could be cached
    1109| 00079|    - String operations in loops
    1110| 00080| 
    1111| 00081| 5. **Maintainability** (INFORMATIONAL)
    1112| 00082|    - Code duplication detection
    1113| 00083|    - Magic number usage (prefer named constants)
    1114| 00084|    - Complex boolean expressions (suggest simplification)
    1115| 00085|

    1118| 00088|    - Memory footprint considerations
    1119| 00089|    - S3 resume path safety

    1222| 00026| 
    1223| 00027| ## Validation Scope: AMI Code Only (MANDATORY Compliance)
    1224| 00028| 
    1225| 00029| These standards are **MANDATORY** for AMI-owned code. Violations impact the final review verdict.
    1226| 00030| 
    1227| 00031| ### File Classification
    1228| 00032| 
    1229| 00033| | File Type | How to Identify | Validation Scope |
    1230| 00034| |-----------|----------------|------------------|
    1231| 00035| | **AMI-owned** | Contains `Copyright (c) 1985-YYYY, AMI` | **Entire file** |
    1232| 00036| | **Third-party with AMI overrides** | Third-party copyright + AMI override markers | **AMI override sections only** |
    1233| 00037| | **No copyright** | No copyright header found | **Entire file** (default to AMI) |
    1234| 00038| | **Third-party only** | Third-party copyright, no AMI markers | **Skip validation** |
    1235| 00039| 
    1236| 00040| ### AMI Override Markers in Third-Party Files
    1237| 00041| 
    1238| 00042| When AMI modifies third-party files (Intel, EDK2, etc.), changes are wrapped in override markers. **Only code between these markers is validated** against AMI organization standards.
    1239| 00043| 
    1240| 00044| **Standard Marker Patterns:**
    1241| 00045| 
    1242| 00046| | Start Marker | End Marker | Usage |
    1243| 00047| |--------------|------------|-------|
    1244| 00048| | `// AMI OVERRIDE START` | `// AMI OVERRIDE END` | General EDK2/Intel file modifications |
    1245| 00049| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_END:` | Server platform overrides |
    1246| 00050| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_END:` | Server platform RC overrides |
    1247| 00051| 
    1248| 00052| **Pattern Recognition (case-insensitive):**
    1249| 00053| ```regex
    1250| 00054| Start: ^\s*//\s*(AMI|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*START
    1251| 00055| End:   ^\s*//\s*(AMI|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*END
    1252| 00056| ```
    1253| 00057| 
    1254| 00058| **Example: Third-Party File with AMI Overrides**
    1255| 00059| 
    1256| 00060| ```c
    1257| 00061| /** @file
    1258| 00062|   Copyright (c) 2020 - 2024, Intel Corporation. All rights reserved.
    1259| 00063|   SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-2-Clause-Patent
    1260| 00064| **/
    1261| 00065| 
    1262| 00066| #include <Uefi.h>
    1263| 00067| 
    1264| 00068| // ⬇️ Third-party code - NOT validated against AMI standards
    1265| 00069| void IntelFunction() {
    1266| 00070|   int bufferSize = 100;  // Raw C types OK in Intel code
    1267| 00071| }
    1268| 00072| 
    1269| 00073| // ⬇️ AMI override section - VALIDATED against AMI standards
    1270| 00074| // AMI OVERRIDE START — Add custom validation
    1271| 00075| BOOLEAN gAmiValidationEnabled = TRUE;  // Must use UEFI types + 'g' prefix
    1272| 00076| 
    1273| 00077| EFI_STATUS AmiCustomValidation(VOID) {  // Must use PascalCase
    1274| 00078|   return EFI_SUCCESS;
    1275| 00079| }
    1276| 00080| // AMI OVERRIDE END
    1277| 00081| // ⬆️ End of AMI code
    1278| 00082| 
    1279| 00083| // ⬇️ Third-party code resumes - NOT validated
    1280| 00084| void AnotherIntelFunction() {
    1281| 00085|   // Intel code continues
    1282| 00086| }
    1283| 00087| ```
    1284| 00088| 
    1285| 00089| **In this example:**
    1286| 00090| - Lines outside override markers: **Not validated** (Intel code)
    1287| 00091| - Lines between `// AMI OVERRIDE START` and `// AMI OVERRIDE END`: **Validated** against all applicable AMI standards (naming, types, patterns)
    1288| 00092| - File header (copyright): **Not validated** (remains Intel copyright)
    1289| 00093| 
    1290| 00094| ---
    1291| 00095| 
    1292| 00096| ## 1. File Header Format
    1293| 00097| 
    1294| 00098| **Applies to:** AMI-owned files only. Third-party files with AMI overrides keep their original header.
    1295| 00099| 
    1296| 00100| Every AMI source file (.c, .h) must use the AMI copyright banner followed by a Doxygen `@file` block:
    1297| 00101| 
    1298| 00102| ```c
    1299| 00103| //***********************************************************************
    1300| 00104| //*                                                                     *
    1301| 00105| //*                 Copyright (c) 1985-20XX, AMI.                       *
    1302| 00106| //*                                                                     *
    1303| 00107| //*      All rights reserved. Subject to AMI licensing agreement.       *
    1304| 00108| //*                                                                     *
    1305| 00109| //***********************************************************************
    1306| 00110| 
    1307| 00111| /** @file ModuleName.c
    1308| 00112|     Brief description of the file's purpose
    1309| 00113| **/
    1310| 00114| ```
    1311| 00115| 
    1312| 00116| ### Requirements
    1313| 00117| - Copyright year must include current year (20XX updated annually) - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if outdated
    1314| 00118| - `@file` block must have file name matching actual file name - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if missing or incorrect
    1315| 00119| - Brief description must be present and meaningful (not "Module file") - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if generic
    1316| 00120| 
    1317| 00121| ---
    1318| 00122| 
    1319| 00123| ## 2. Source File Organization
    1320| 00124| 
    1321| 00125| Files are organized with `//------` separator lines into sections in this **strict order**:
    1322| 00126| 
    1323| 00127| ### Section Order (Mandatory)
    1324| 00128| 
    1325| 00129| 1. **Include(s)**
    1326| 00130| 2. **Constant, Macro and Type Definition(s)**
    1327| 00131|    - Sub-groups: Constant, Macro, Type, Function Prototype
    1328| 00132| 3. **Variable and External Declaration(s)**
    1329| 00133|    - Sub-groups: Variable, GUID, Protocol/PPI, External, Function definitions
    1330| 00134| 
    1331| 00135| ### Example Structure
    1332| 00136| 
    1333| 00137| ```c
    1334| 00138| //***********************************************************************
    1335| 00139| // Copyright & @file block
    1336| 00140| //***********************************************************************
    1337| 00141| 
    1338| 00142| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1339| 00143| // Include(s)
    1340| 00144| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1341| 00145| #include <Uefi.h>
    1342| 00146| #include <Token.h>
    1343| 00147| #include <AmiDxeLib.h>
    1344| 00148| 
    1345| 00149| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1346| 00150| // Constant, Macro and Type Definition(s)
    1347| 00151| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1348| 00152| 
    1349| 00153| // Constant Definition(s)
    1350| 00154| #define MAX_BUFFER_SIZE  256
    1351| 00155| 
    1352| 00156| // Macro Definition(s)
    1353| 00157| #define GET_ELEMENT(x)  ((x) & 0xFF)
    1354| 00158| 
    1355| 00159| // Type Definition(s)
    1356| 00160| typedef struct {
    1357| 00161|   UINT32  Field1;
    1358| 00162|   UINT16  Field2;
    1359| 00163| } MY_STRUCTURE;
    1360| 00164| 
    1361| 00165| // Function Prototype(s)
    1362| 00166| EFI_STATUS InitializeModule(VOID);
    1363| 00167| 
    1364| 00168| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1365| 00169| // Variable and External Declaration(s)
    1366| 00170| //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1367| 00171| 
    1368| 00172| // Variable Declaration(s)
    1369| 00173| STATIC UINT8  mLocalBuffer[MAX_BUFFER_SIZE];
    1370| 00174| 
    1371| 00175| // GUID Definition(s)
    1372| 00176| EFI_GUID gMyProtocolGuid = MY_PROTOCOL_GUID;
    1373| 00177| 
    1374| 00178| // Protocol/PPI Declaration(s)
    1375| 00179| MY_PROTOCOL  *gMyProtocol = NULL;
    1376| 00180| 
    1377| 00181| // External Declaration(s)
    1378| 00182| extern UINT32  gExternalValue;
    1379| 00183| 
    1380| 00184| // Function Definition(s)
    1381| 00185| EFI_STATUS
    1382| 00186| InitializeModule (
    1383| 00187|   VOID
    1384| 00188|   )
    1385| 00189| {
    1386| 00190|   // Implementation
    1387| 00191| }
    1388| 00192| ```
    1389| 00193| 
    1390| 00194| ---
    1391| 00195| 
    1392| 00196| ## 3. Naming Conventions
    1393| 00197| 
    1394| 00198| ### Raw C Types (MANDATORY-MAJOR)
    1395| 00199| 
    1396| 00200| **NEVER use raw C types** — they cause ABI incompatibility, platform-dependent sizes, and runtime failures.
    1397| 00201| 
    1398| 00202| | ❌ Prohibited (Raw C) | ✅ Required (UEFI) | Reason |
    1399| 00203| |---------------------|-------------------|---------|
    1400| 00204| | `int` | `UINT32` or `INT32` | Size varies (16/32 bits) |
    1401| 00205| | `unsigned` | `UINT32` or `UINTN` | Platform-dependent |
    1402| 00206| | `char` | `CHAR8` | Sign varies by compiler |
    1403| 00207| | `void` | `VOID` | UEFI convention |
    1404| 00208| | `long` | `UINT64` or `INT64` | Size varies (32/64 bits) |
    1405| 00209| | `short` | `UINT16` or `INT16` | Not portable |
    1406| 00210| 
    1407| 00211| **Examples of MANDATORY-MAJOR violations:**
    1408| 00212| ```c
    1409| 00213| // ❌ WRONG - Raw C types
    1410| 00214| int bufferSize = 100;
    1411| 00215| char name[64];
    1412| 00216| unsigned index;
    1413| 00217| void *ptr;
    1414| 00218| extern int VfrBin[];
    1415| 00219| 
    1416| 00220| // ✅ CORRECT - UEFI types
    1417| 00221| UINT32 BufferSize = 100;
    1418| 00222| CHAR8 Name[64];
    1419| 00223| UINTN Index;
    1420| 00224| VOID *Ptr;
    1421| 00225| extern UINT8 VfrBin[];
    1422| 00226| ```
    1423| 00227| 
    1424| 00228| **Severity:** **MANDATORY-MAJOR** — Treated as MAJOR finding in main review; may trigger CONDITIONAL APPROVE or BLOCK verdict.
    1425| 00229| 
    1426| 00230| ---
    1427| 00231| 
    1428| 00232| ### Functions
    1429| 00233| 
    1430| 00234| | Pattern | Convention | Example |
    1431| 00235| |---------|-----------|---------|
    1432| 00236| | General functions | PascalCase | `InitializeDriver`, `ProcessBuffer` |
    1433| 00237| | Entry points | `<Module>Init` or `<Module>EntryPoint` | `CrbDxeInit`, `SmbiosPeiInit` |
    1434| 00238| | Static/local functions | PascalCase (prefix optional) | `ValidateInput`, `LocalHelper` |
    1435| 00239| 
    1436| 00240| ### Variables
    1437| 00241| 
    1438| 00242| | Pattern | Convention | Example |
    1439| 00243| |---------|-----------|---------|
    1440| 00244| | Global variables | `g` prefix + PascalCase | `gBootScript`, `gAmiCrbInfoPpi` |
    1441| 00245| | Registration variables | `g<Name>Reg` | `gAmiConOutStartedProtocolReg` |
    1442| 00246| | Module-scope static | `m` prefix + PascalCase | `mLocalBuffer`, `mInitialized` |
    1443| 00247| | Local variables | camelCase or PascalCase | `BufferSize`, `status` |
    1444| 00248| 
    1445| 00249| ### Constants and Macros
    1446| 00250| 
    1447| 00251| - ALL_CAPS with underscores: `MAX_BUFFER_SIZE`, `ENABLE_DEBUG_MODE`
    1448| 00252| - Token names in SDL: ALL_CAPS with underscores: `DEBUG_MODE`, `CRB_BOARD`
    1449| 00253| 
    1450| 00254| ### Types
    1451| 00255| 
    1452| 00256| - UEFI types: `EFI_STATUS`, `VOID`, `UINT8`, `UINT16`, `UINT32`, `UINT64`, `UINTN`, `BOOLEAN`, `EFI_HANDLE`
    1453| 00257| - Custom types: PascalCase with all-caps suffix: `MY_PROTOCOL`, `SETUP_DATA`, `GPIO_CONFIG`
    1454| 00258| - Pointer types: use UEFI style: `EFI_HANDLE *Handle` (not `EFI_HANDLE* Handle`)
    1455| 00259| 
    1456| 00260| ---
    1457| 00261| 
    1458| 00262| ## 4. Include Order
    1459| 00263| 
    1460| 00264| Includes must follow this order:
    1461| 00265| 
    1462| 00266| ```c
    1463| 00267| #include <Uefi.h>       // or <Pei.h> for PEI modules - FIRST
    1464| 00268| #include <Token.h>       // auto-generated SDL token definitions
    1465| 00269| #include <AmiDxeLib.h>   // AMI DXE library (or <AmiPeiLib.h> for PEI)
    1466| 00270| #include <Library/PcdLib.h>       // EDK2 standard libraries
    1467| 00271| #include <Library/BaseMemoryLib.h>
    1468| 00272| #include <Protocol/SomeProtocol.h> // Protocol / PPI headers
    1469| 00273| #include <SetupVariable.h>         // Platform-specific headers
    1470| 00274| ```
    1471| 00275| 
    1472| 00276| ### Rules
    1473| 00277| 1. **Phase header first:** `<Uefi.h>` or `<Pei.h>` or `<Base.h>`
    1474| 00278| 2. **AMI headers next:** `<Token.h>`, `<AmiDxeLib.h>` / `<AmiPeiLib.h>`
    1475| 00279| 3. **EDK2 libraries:** `<Library/...>`
    1476| 00280| 4. **Protocol/PPI/GUID headers:** `<Protocol/...>`, `<Ppi/...>`, `<Guid/...>`
    1477| 00281| 5. **Platform headers last:** Setup, board-specific
    1478| 00282| 
    1479| 00283| ---
    1480| 00284| 
    1481| 00285| ## 5. INF File Structure
    1482| 00286| 
    1483| 00287| INF file sections must appear in this order:
    1484| 00288| 
    1485| 00289| ```ini
    1486| 00290| [Defines]
    1487| 00291|   INF_VERSION                    = 0x00010005
    1488| 00292|   BASE_NAME                      = ModuleName
    1489| 00293|   FILE_GUID                      = XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX
    1490| 00294|   MODULE_TYPE                    = DXE_DRIVER
    1491| 00295|   VERSION_STRING                 = 1.0
    1492| 00296|   ENTRY_POINT                    = ModuleInit
    1493| 00297| 
    1494| 00298| [Sources]
    1495| 00299|   ModuleFile.c
    1496| 00300|   ModuleHeader.h
    1497| 00301| 
    1498| 00302| [Packages]
    1499| 00303|   MdePkg/MdePkg.dec              # MUST be first
    1500| 00304|   AmiModulePkg/AmiModulePkg.dec
    1501| 00305|   AmiChipsetModulePkg/AmiChipsetModulePkg.dec
    1502| 00306| 
    1503| 00307| [LibraryClasses]
    1504| 00308|   UefiDriverEntryPoint           # Entry point library
    1505| 00309|   UefiBootServicesTableLib
    1506| 00310|   BaseMemoryLib
    1507| 00311| 
    1508| 00312| [Protocols]
    1509| 00313|   gEfiSomeProtocolGuid           # PRODUCED
    1510| 00314|   gEfiOtherProtocolGuid          # CONSUMED
    1511| 00315| 
    1512| 00316| [Guids]
    1513| 00317|   gEfiEventGroupGuid
    1514| 00318| 
    1515| 00319| [Pcd]
    1516| 00320|   gEfiMdePkgTokenSpaceGuid.PcdSomeValue
    1517| 00321| 
    1518| 00322| [Depex]
    1519| 00323|   gEfiSomeProtocolGuid AND gEfiOtherProtocolGuid
    1520| 00324| ```
    1521| 00325| 
    1522| 00326| ### Requirements
    1523| 00327| - `MdePkg/MdePkg.dec` must be **first** in `[Packages]` - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if not first
    1524| 00328| - Entry-point library must be **first** in `[LibraryClasses]` - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if not first
    1525| 00329| - Section order must match above - **MANDATORY-MINOR** if out of order
    1526| 00330| - Comment PRODUCED vs CONSUMED for protocols/PPIs when not obvious
    1527| 00331| 
    1528| 00332| ---
    1529| 00333| 
    1530| 00334| ## 6. AMI Override Marker Policy
    1531| 00335| 
    1532| 00336| `// AMI OVERRIDE START/END` markers are **required only** when modifying EDK2 or Intel-owned files. They are **never** used in AMI-owned packages.
    1533| 00337| 
    1534| 00338| ### When Markers are Required
    1535| 00339| 
    1536| 00340| | Package path | Markers required? | Violation if missing |
    1537| 00341| |---|---|---|
    1538| 00342| | `Intel/` (any Intel package) | ✅ **YES** | **MANDATORY-MAJOR** |
    1539| 00343| | `MdePkg/`, `MdeModulePkg/`, `SecurityPkg/`, `CryptoPkg/`, `UefiCpuPkg/` | ✅ **YES** | **MANDATORY-MAJOR** |
    1540| 00344| | `Ami*Pkg/`, `CrbPkg/`, `AmiCrbPkg/`, vendor packages | ❌ **NO** | N/A |
    1541| 00345| 
    1542| 00346| ### Syntax (EDK2 / Intel files only)
    1543| 00347| 
    1544| 00348| ```c
    1545| 00349| // AMI OVERRIDE START — <brief description> (<YYYY-MM-DD>)
    1546| 00350| ... changed code ...
    1547| 00351| // AMI OVERRIDE END
    1548| 00352| ```
    1549| 00353| 
    1550| 00354| **Example:**
    1551| 00355| ```c
    1552| 00356| // AMI OVERRIDE START — Add SMRAM boundary validation (2026-05-15)
    1553| 00357| if (Address < mSmramBase || Address > mSmramEnd) {
    1554| 00358|   return EFI_ACCESS_DENIED;
    1555| 00359| }
    1556| 00360| // AMI OVERRIDE END
    1557| 00361| ```
    1558| 00362| 
    1559| 00363| ---
    1560| 00364| 
    1561| 00365| ## 7. SDL Token Patterns
    1562| 00366| 
    1563| 00367| ### Token Declaration
    1564| 00368| 
    1565| 00369| ```sdl
    1566| 00370| TOKEN
    1567| 00371|     Name  = "MY_FEATURE_ENABLE"
    1568| 00372|     Value  = "1"
    1569| 00373|     Help  = "Enable my feature support"
    1570| 00374|     TokenType = Boolean
    1571| 00375|     TargetMAK = Yes
    1572| 00376|     TargetH = Yes
    1573| 00377| End
    1574| 00378| ```
    1575| 00379| 
    1576| 00380| ### Token Override (Higher Layer)
    1577| 00381| 
    1578| 00382| ```sdl
    1579| 00383| TOKEN
    1580| 00384|     Name  = "MY_FEATURE_ENABLE"
    1581| 00385|     Value  = "0"
    1582| 00386|     TokenType = Boolean
    1583| 00387|     TargetMAK = Yes
    1584| 00388|     TargetH = Yes
    1585| 00389| End
    1586| 00390| ```
    1587| 00391| 
    1588| 00392| ### PCD Mapping
    1589| 00393| 
    1590| 00394| ```sdl
    1591| 00395| PcdMapping
    1592| 00396|     Name  = "PcdMyValue"
    1593| 00397|     GuidSpace  = "gMyTokenSpaceGuid"
    1594| 00398|     PcdType  = "PcdsFixedAtBuild"
    1595| 00399|     DataType  = "Uint32"
    1596| 00400|     Value  = "$(MY_TOKEN_VALUE)"
    1597| 00401|     TargetDSC = Yes
    1598| 00402| End
    1599| 00403| ```
    1600| 00404| 
    1601| 00405| ---
    1602| 00406| 
    1603| 00407| ## 8. ELINK Patterns
    1604| 00408| 
    1605| 00409| ### ELINK Chain Root (Owning Module)
    1606| 00410| 
    1607| 00411| ```sdl
    1608| 00412| ELINK
    1609| 00413|     Name  = "MyHandlerList"
    1610| 00414|     InvokeOrder = ReplaceParent
    1611| 00415| End
    1612| 00416| ```
    1613| 00417| 
    1614| 00418| ### ELINK Registration (Contributor)
    1615| 00419| 
    1616| 00420| ```sdl
    1617| 00421| ELINK
    1618| 00422|     Name  = "MyHookFunction,"          # Note trailing comma
    1619| 00423|     Parent  = "MyHandlerList"
    1620| 00424|     InvokeOrder = AfterParent
    1621| 00425| End
    1622| 00426| ```
    1623| 00427| 
    1624| 00428| ### Function Typedef (Owning Module Header)
    1625| 00429| 
    1626| 00430| ```c
    1627| 00431| typedef VOID (MY_HANDLER_HOOK) (UINT8 Data, UINT64 Parameter);
    1628| 00432| ```
    1629| 00433| 
    1630| 00434| ### Consumption (Owning Module .c)
    1631| 00435| 
    1632| 00436| ```c
    1633| 00437| #include <MyModuleELinks.h>
    1634| 00438| 
    1635| 00439| extern MY_HANDLER_HOOK MY_HANDLER_LIST EndOfList;
    1636| 00440| MY_HANDLER_HOOK* MyHandlers[] = {MY_HANDLER_LIST NULL};
    1637| 00441| ```
    1638| 00442| 
    1639| 00443| ---
    1640| 00444| 
    1641| 00445| ## 9. Customization Layers
    1642| 00446| 
    1643| 00447| Changes should target the **outermost applicable layer**:
    1644| 00448| 
    1645| 00449| ```
    1646| 00450| ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    1647| 00451| │  <project>.sdl           (project overrides)    │
    1648| 00452| ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    1649| 00453| │  <VendorPkg>/            (vendor/OEM custom)    │
    1650| 00454| ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    1651| 00455| │  CrbPkg/ or AmiCrbPkg/   (board reference)      │
    1652| 00456| ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    1653| 00457| │  AmiModulePkg/           (AMI core - modify OK) │
    1654| 00458| ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    1655| 00459| │  Intel/                  (use AMI OVERRIDE)     │
    1656| 00460| ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    1657| 00461| │  MdePkg / MdeModulePkg   (use AMI OVERRIDE)     │
    1658| 00462| └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    1659| 00463| ```
    1660| 00464| 
    1661| 00465| ### Rules
    1662| 00466| - Prefer SDL token overrides over code patches
    1663| 00467| - Use ELINK hooks instead of modifying original module source
    1664| 00468| - Vendor package customizations override CRB package
    1665| 00469| - Never modify `Build/` or `Conf/` files (auto-generated)
    1666| 00470| 
    1667| 00471| ---
    1668| 00472| 
    1669| 00473| ## 10. Module Type Specific Patterns
    1670| 00474| 
    1671| 00475| ### PEI Module Entry Point

    1755| 00559| ## Validation Checklist
    1756| 00560| 
    1757| 00561| When reviewing code for AMI organization standards compliance:
    1758| 00562| 
    1759| 00563| ☐ **File Header**
    1760| 00564|   - [ ] AMI copyright banner present
    1761| 00565|   - [ ] Current year in copyright
    1762| 00566|   - [ ] `@file` block with correct filename and description
    1763| 00567| 
    1764| 00568| ☐ **File Organization**
    1765| 00569|   - [ ] Sections in correct order (Include, Constant/Macro/Type, Variable/External)
    1766| 00570|   - [ ] `//------` separators present
    1767| 00571|   - [ ] Include order follows AMI pattern
    1768| 00572| 
    1769| 00573| ☐ **Naming**
    1770| 00574|   - [ ] Functions use PascalCase
    1771| 00575|   - [ ] Entry points use `<Module>Init` pattern
    1772| 00576|   - [ ] Global variables use `g` prefix
    1773| 00577|   - [ ] Constants use ALL_CAPS
    1774| 00578|   - [ ] No raw C types (`int`, `char`, `void`)
    1775| 00579| 
    1776| 00580| ☐ **INF Structure**
    1777| 00581|   - [ ] Sections in correct order
    1778| 00582|   - [ ] `MdePkg/MdePkg.dec` first in `[Packages]`
    1779| 00583|   - [ ] Entry-point library first in `[LibraryClasses]`
    1780| 00584| 
    1781| 00585| ☐ **Customization Layer**
    1782| 00586|   - [ ] Changes in appropriate layer (outermost)
    1783| 00587|   - [ ] AMI OVERRIDE markers used correctly (Intel/EDK2 only)
    1784| 00588|   - [ ] SDL tokens preferred over code patches
    1785| 00589| 
    1786| 00590| ☐ **AMI Patterns**
    1787| 00591|   - [ ] ELINK registrations have trailing comma
    1788| 00592|   - [ ] Setup variable access uses proper pattern
    1789| 00593|   - [ ] Boot script macros used correctly
    1790| 00594|

    1810| 00008| # AMI Module Developer's Guide Standards Validation (MANDATORY)
    1811| 00009| 
    1812| 00010| ## Purpose
    1813| 00011| Validate reviewed code against **mandatory** AMI Aptio 5.x Module Developer's Guide standards that extend beyond UEFI 2.10+, PI 1.8+, and EDK II C Coding Standard 2.2+ requirements.
    1814| 00012| 
    1815| 00013| **Compliance Level:** MANDATORY - Violations impact the final review verdict and may trigger CONDITIONAL APPROVE or BLOCK.
    1816| 00014| 
    1817| 00015| ## When to Use
    1818| 00016| - **At the end of UEFI code review** (after Stage 3 verdict is written)
    1819| 00017| - To check AMI-specific organization coding standards
    1820| 00018| - Only on files that were already reviewed for UEFI/PI/EDK2 compliance
    1821| 00019| 
    1822| 00020| ## Scope
    1823| 00021| This skill checks **AMI-specific mandatory** patterns only. UEFI/PI/EDK2 spec compliance is already covered by the main review stages.
    1824| 00022| 
    1825| 00023| ## Standards Reference
    1826| 00024| See [AMI Module Developer Standards](./Module_Developer_Standards.md) for complete mandatory organization requirements.
    1827| 00025| 
    1828| 00026| ## Validation Procedure
    1829| 00027| 
    1830| 00028| ### Step 1: Identify Files in Scope
    1831| 00029| Review only files that were checked in the main review (listed in `cc_registry.md` with Review Status ≠ `NA`). Do not review files that were skipped or excluded.
    1832| 00030| 
    1833| 00031| ### Step 2: Classify File Ownership (AMI vs Third-Party)
    1834| 00032| 
    1835| 00033| For each in-scope file, determine ownership by reading the file header (first 50 lines):
    1836| 00034| 
    1837| 00035| **Classification Rules:**
    1838| 00036| 
    1839| 00037| | Condition | Classification | Validation Scope |
    1840| 00038| |-----------|----------------|------------------|
    1841| 00039| | File contains AMI copyright banner (`Copyright (c) 1985-20XX, AMI`) | ✅ **AMI-owned** | Entire file |
    1842| 00040| | File contains third-party copyright (Intel, Microsoft, EDK2, etc.) AND contains AMI override markers | ⚙️ **Third-party with AMI overrides** | AMI override sections only |
    1843| 00041| | File contains NO copyright header | ✅ **AMI-owned** (default assumption) | Entire file |
    1844| 00042| | File contains only third-party copyright, NO AMI override markers | ❌ **Third-party only** | Skip validation |
    1845| 00043| 
    1846| 00044| **AMI Override Marker Patterns (case-insensitive):**
    1847| 00045| 
    1848| 00046| Detect AMI-owned code sections in third-party files using these marker patterns:
    1849| 00047| 
    1850| 00048| | Start Marker | End Marker | Purpose |
    1851| 00049| |--------------|------------|---------|
    1852| 00050| | `// AMI OVERRIDE START` | `// AMI OVERRIDE END` | General EDK2/Intel overrides |
    1853| 00051| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_END:` | Server platform overrides |
    1854| 00052| | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_START:` | `//APTIOV_SERVER_OVERRIDE_RC_END:` | Server platform RC overrides |
    1855| 00053| | Any marker matching: `//<PREFIX>OVERRIDE*START` where PREFIX contains "AMI" or "APTIOV" | Corresponding `END` marker | Project-specific AMI override tags |
    1856| 00054| 
    1857| 00055| **Detection Pattern:**
    1858| 00056| ```regex
    1859| 00057| Start: ^\s*//\s*(AMI|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*START
    1860| 00058| End:   ^\s*//\s*(AMI|APTIOV)[A-Z_]*OVERRIDE[A-Z_]*END
    1861| 00059| ```
    1862| 00060| 
    1863| 00061| **Copyright Detection Patterns:**
    1864| 00062| - AMI: `Copyright (c) 1985-YYYY, AMI` or `Copyright.*AMI`
    1865| 00063| - Intel: `Copyright.*Intel Corporation`
    1866| 00064| - Microsoft: `Copyright.*Microsoft Corporation`
    1867| 00065| - EDK2/TianoCore: `Copyright.*TianoCore`
    1868| 00066| 
    1869| 00067| ### Step 3: Extract AMI Code Sections
    1870| 00068| 
    1871| 00069| For each file, extract the relevant code based on classification:
    1872| 00070| 
    1873| 00071| **AMI-owned files (entire file validation):**
    1874| 00072| - Read full file content
    1875| 00073| - Validate all sections against AMI organization standards
    1876| 00074| - Apply all checks from Step 4
    1877| 00075| 
    1878| 00076| **Third-party files with AMI overrides (section-only validation):**
    1879| 00077| - Parse file line-by-line
    1880| 00078| - Extract ONLY lines between AMI override START/END markers (inclusive)
    1881| 00079| - Validate extracted sections only
    1882| 00080| - Report findings with original file line numbers
    1883| 00081| - Record: `[Third-party file — validating AMI override sections only]`
    1884| 00082| 
    1885| 00083| **Third-party files without AMI code:**
    1886| 00084| - Skip validation entirely
    1887| 00085| - Record: `[SKIP: Third-party file, no AMI code sections detected]`
    1888| 00086| 
    1889| 00087| **Examples:**
    1890| 00088| 
    1891| 00089| ```c
    1892| 00090| // Intel copyright header
    1893| 00091| // ...
    1894| 00092| void IntelFunction() {
    1895| 00093|   // Skip this - third-party code
    1896| 00094| }
    1897| 00095| 
    1898| 00096| // AMI OVERRIDE START — Add custom validation
    1899| 00097| BOOLEAN gAmiCustomFlag = FALSE;  // ← Validate this (AMI code)
    1900| 00098| 
    1901| 00099| EFI_STATUS ValidateCustom() {   // ← Validate this (AMI code)
    1902| 00100|   return EFI_SUCCESS;
    1903| 00101| }
    1904| 00102| // AMI OVERRIDE END
    1905| 00103| 
    1906| 00104| void AnotherIntelFunction() {
    1907| 00105|   // Skip this - third-party code
    1908| 00106| }
    1909| 00107| ```
    1910| 00108| 
    1911| 00109| ### Step 4: Check Organization Standards
    1912| 00110| 
    1913| 00111| For each AMI code section (entire file OR extracted override blocks), verify:
    1914| 00112| 
    1915| 00113| 1. **File Header Format** (AMI-owned files only)
    1916| 00114|    - AMI copyright banner present and current year (2026)
    1917| 00115|    - Doxygen `@file` block with brief description
    1918| 00116|    - Skip for third-party files with overrides (header is third-party)
    1919| 00117| 
    1920| 00118| 2. **Source File Organization** (all AMI code)
    1921| 00119|    - Sections in correct order with `//------` separators (AMI files only)
    1922| 00120|    - Include order follows AMI pattern (when includes are in AMI section)
    1923| 00121| 
    1924| 00122| 3. **Naming Conventions** (all AMI code) - MANDATORY
    1925| 00123|    - Functions: PascalCase
    1926| 00124|    - Entry points: `<Module>Init` pattern
    1927| 00125|    - Global variables: `g` prefix + PascalCase
    1928| 00126|    - Registration variables: `g<Name>Reg` pattern
    1929| 00127|    - Constants/Macros: ALL_CAPS
    1930| 00128|    - **No raw C types** (`int`, `char`, `void`) - **MANDATORY-MAJOR violation if present**
    1931| 00129| 
    1932| 00130| 4. **INF File Structure** (AMI-owned INF files only)
    1933| 00131|    - Sections in AMI-specified order
    1934| 00132|    - `MdePkg/MdePkg.dec` listed first in `[Packages]`
    1935| 00133|    - Skip for third-party INF files
    1936| 00134| 
    1937| 00135| 5. **AMI-Specific Patterns** (all AMI code)
    1938| 00136|    - SDL token usage
    1939| 00137|    - ELINK patterns (when modified)
    1940| 00138|    - Customization layer compliance
    1941| 00139| 
    1942| 00140| ### Step 5: Report Findings

    2140| 00008| # Build Log Analyzer
    2141| 00009| 
    2142| 00010| ## Purpose
    2143| 00011| Efficiently locate the **root cause failure point** in a build.log without loading the entire file.
    2144| 00012| Uses streaming grep — safe for very large logs (>100 MB).
    2145| 00013| 
    2146| 00014| ## When to Use
    2147| 00015| - User says "build failed" or "check build.log"
    2148| 00016| - Need to find which module/file caused the first error
    2149| 00017| - AMI/UEFI EDKII build log analysis
    2150| 00018| - TypeScript `tsc` error extraction
    2151| 00019| - npm / Node.js / make build failures
    2152| 00020| 
    2153| 00021| ## Procedure
    2154| 00022| 
    2155| 00023| ### Step 1 — Locate the log file
    2156| 00024| Check these paths in order (stop at first match):
    2157| 00025| 1. Argument provided by user
    2158| 00026| 2. `Build.log` (workspace root, case-insensitive)
    2159| 00027| 3. `build/Build.log`
    2160| 00028| 4. `out/build.log`
    2161| 00029| 5. Ask the user if none found
    2162| 00030| 
    2163| 00031| Use `file_search` with pattern `**/Build.log` or `**/build.log`.
    2164| 00032| 
    2165| 00033| ### Step 2 — Stream-scan for errors (DO NOT read the whole file)
    2166| 00034| Run the PowerShell script: [find-errors.ps1](./scripts/find-errors.ps1)
    2167| 00035| 
    2168| 00036| ```powershell
    2169| 00037| # Quick invocation:
    2170| 00038| & "C:\Users\YCHsu\.github\skills\build-log-analyzer\scripts\find-errors.ps1" -LogPath "<path>"
    2171| 00039| ```
    2172| 00040| 
    2173| 00041| Or use `grep_search` with these patterns (isRegexp=true):
    2174| 00042| - `error [A-Z]|error:|ERROR|FAILED|Build FAILED|make\[.*\] \*\*\*`
    2175| 00043| - For TypeScript: `error TS\d+:`
    2176| 00044| - For EDKII/AMI: `ERROR - |Module .* failed|FAILED - `
    2177| 00045| 
    2178| 00046| ### Step 3 — Find the ROOT CAUSE (first error)
    2179| 00047| 1. Identify the **earliest** error line in the file (lowest line number)
    2180| 00048| 2. Read ±10 lines of context around that first error using `read_file`
    2181| 00049| 3. Distinguish: root cause error vs cascading/downstream errors
    2182| 00050| 
    2183| 00051| ### Step 4 — Report
    2184| 00052| Structure the output as:
    2185| 00053|

    2188| 00056| 
    2189| 00057| **Root Cause** (line N):
    2190| 00058| <error message>
    2191| 00059| <context>
    2192| 00060| 
    2193| 00061| **Error Count**: N errors total
    2194| 00062| **Error Types**: [tsc | make | AMI module | linker | etc.]
    2195| 00063| 
    2196| 00064| **Cascading Errors** (if any): N additional errors likely caused by above
    2197| 00065| ```
    2198| 00066| 
    2199| 00067| ## Error Pattern Reference
    2200| 00068| 
    2201| 00069| | Build System | Key Patterns |
    2202| 00070| |---|---|
    2203| 00071| | TypeScript tsc | `error TS\d+:`, `Found \d+ error` |
    2204| 00072| | AMI/EDKII | `ERROR - `, `FAILED - stopping`, `make[N]: ***`, `Build FAILED` |

    2207| 00075| | GCC/Clang | `error:.*\[-W`, `: error:` |

    2209| 00077| 
    2210| 00078| ## Important Rules
    2211| 00079| - **NEVER** use `read_file` on the entire log — use `grep_search` + targeted `read_file` for context only
    2212| 00080| - Report the **first** error, not the last
